entries.title: The math quiz with the hard last question
entries.body: So today in math Mr. Dawson gave us a quiz on adding big numbers with regrouping. It was so boring for most of it because we had to show our work, and showing your work takes forever. But the last question was a word problem about a guy with 347 Pokemon cards and I knew it right away. I got a 9 out of 10! I only missed one because I forgot to carry the one. Jack got a 10, so I was kind of mad. Okay, really mad.
entries.highlight: Got 9 out of 10 on a math quiz and was a little frustrated that Jack beat him.

entries.title: Mom's new homework first rule
entries.body: I had so much homework today. A whole page of spelling and a math sheet and reading for twenty minutes. Mom made a new rule. It is homework first, then games. I said that is not fair because Friday is supposed to be a free day, and she said Friday is still a day. Then she said she wants me to study so I can go to college someday. I don't even know what college is like. I finished it all before dinner but I was grumpy the whole time.
entries.highlight: Mom introduced a homework-first rule, and he grumbled but finished everything before dinner.

entries.title: Jack's trampoline birthday
entries.body: I went to Jack's birthday party at the trampoline park. He turned nine. There was a giant foam pit and me and Jack jumped in it like fifty times. Owen got stuck at the bottom and we had to pull him out by his arms. Then we had cake and I ate three pieces. Well, two and a half, because Tessa was not there so nobody stole any. I gave Jack a pack of Pokemon cards and he got a holo on the first try.
entries.highlight: Celebrated Jack's ninth birthday at a trampoline park and jumped in the foam pit with friends.

entries.title: No screens and the couch cushion hideout
entries.body: There was no school today because of Thanksgiving tomorrow. Mom said no video games all day because I played too much yesterday. So I built a hideout out of all the couch cushions and two blankets and the dining chairs. Tessa wanted to come in and I said no because it was a boys only hideout. She threw a fit and cried. Then Mom made me let her in. Honestly the hideout was okay but I wish it was nighttime so the day would be over.
entries.highlight: Built a couch-cushion hideout during a no-screens day, though he did not want to share it with Tessa.

entries.title: Jafie beat me at Pokemon again
entries.body: Jafie came over the day after Thanksgiving and we played Pokemon on the Switch. We did battles with our own teams. My team had Charizard and Gengar and I thought I was gonna win for sure. But Jafie beat me in the last one with a Pikachu. A Pikachu! I said he was cheating and he said he was not. I was so mad I put the controller down really hard. Mom said one more hour and then outside. We ate leftover pie on the porch after.
entries.highlight: Lost a Pokemon battle to Jafie and got upset, accusing him of cheating.

entries.title: Card shop Saturday with Dad
entries.body: Dad took me to the card shop downtown. It is called Game Haven and it smells like old books and pizza. On Saturdays kids battle with their Pokemon cards at the long tables. I played a kid named Ruben and lost, then I played a girl with a water deck and I won! Dad bought me one booster pack. I got a shiny Snorlax. I am gonna keep it in the front of my binder so everybody sees it.
entries.highlight: Played Pokemon card battles at a local card shop and got a shiny Snorlax from a booster pack.

entries.title: Tessa took my game cartridge
entries.body: My sister was so annoying today. Tessa is five and she went in my room and took my Pokemon game cartridge and hid it in her purse. I looked for it for like a whole hour. Then she said it was a game and I had to find it. I yelled and she threw a fit and Mom said we both had to take a break. Then later we played Go Fish and she won, which was weird. I am still mad about the cartridge though.
entries.highlight: Got frustrated when Tessa hid his game, but they ended the day playing Go Fish together.

entries.title: Beat the Elite Four with Mateo watching
entries.body: Mateo came over after school and we played Pokemon. I was stuck on the Elite Four for like two weeks. Mateo helped me make a better team because he knows a lot about types. He said use ice moves on the dragon lady. I tried it and I won! I beat the whole Elite Four and became the champion! We screamed so loud Mom came running in. It was the best day of my life, at least this week.
entries.highlight: Beat the Elite Four in his Pokemon game for the first time after getting team advice from Mateo.

entries.title: Socks under my bed
entries.body: I had to clean my room. Mom said it looked like a tornado lived in there. I found three missing socks under the bed and a granola bar that was super old and squished. Gross. I also found my Lego guy that I lost in like first grade. It took forever, like six hours. Not really, maybe forty minutes. Mom said I did a good job and I could play games for thirty minutes after. It was worth it I guess.
entries.highlight: Cleaned his messy room, found long-lost socks and a toy, and earned some game time.

entries.title: Tessa wants her own cards
entries.body: Me and Dad played Pokemon cards on the kitchen table after lunch. Dad is not very good at it because he plays Magic too much and he gets the rules mixed up. Tessa wanted to play too, so I gave her my worst cards, like the Caterpie and stuff. She did not know how to play and she just made the cards talk to each other. That is not how it works. But Dad thought it was funny. I won two times.
entries.highlight: Played Pokemon cards with Dad and let Tessa have some of his extra cards.

entries.title: Carpool jingle bells
entries.body: In carpool this morning everybody was singing Jingle Bells really loud but the Batman version. Jack's mom drives us in her big minivan and she let us do it even though it was so loud. Mateo did the high part and his voice cracked and we laughed so hard. Owen said he felt a little sick from laughing. Nobody puked though. We got to school right when the bell rang.
entries.highlight: Sang holiday songs with friends in Jack's mom's minivan on the way to school.

entries.title: Biscuit the puppy at Eli's
entries.body: I went to Eli's house after school. His dog is named Biscuit and she is a golden puppy and she is so crazy. She chewed up one of Eli's shoes while we were playing Minecraft and Eli's mom was mad. We took Biscuit in the backyard and threw a tennis ball. She kept bringing it back all slobbery. I want a dog so bad but Mom says no because Tessa is allergic. Maybe when I am eleven.
entries.highlight: Played with Eli's puppy Biscuit after school and wished for a dog of his own.

entries.title: Owen's basement Lego city
entries.body: I went to Owen's house after school. Owen has a basement and it has a whole Lego city on a big table. His big brother built most of it but we are allowed to play with the cars part. We made a police chase and the robber car crashed into the pizza shop. Owen's mom made us grilled cheese. Owen is kind of quiet at school but at his house he is super funny.
entries.highlight: Played with a big Lego city at Owen's house and noticed Owen is funnier at home.

entries.title: Freezing hands at the hoop
entries.body: Me and Eli played basketball at the park even though it was freezing. Our hands were so cold the ball felt like a rock. We played HORSE and Eli won because he can do a trick shot from behind the bench. I said that one does not count. Then we just shot free throws until Eli's mom honked. I made six in a row which is my record. My fingers are still red.
entries.favorite: Six free throws in a row
entries.highlight: Played basketball in the cold with Eli and set a personal record of six free throws in a row.

entries.title: Card battles at Grandma's table
entries.body: At night we went to Grandma's for an early Christmas dinner and I brought my Pokemon binder. My cousin Danny is twelve and he has really good cards. We battled on Grandma's table after dinner. He beat me two times but on the third time I used my Snorlax and won. Danny said good job. I said I know. Grandma made us stop because we were too loud.
entries.highlight: Battled Pokemon cards with his older cousin at Grandma's and won one of three games.

entries.title: Christmas and the karaoke machine of doom
entries.body: Christmas! I woke up at six and Mom said go back to bed. I did not. I got the new Mario Kart game and a bike helmet with flames on it. It is so cool, it looks like a race car. Dad got me a new fishing pole too. Tessa got a karaoke machine. Oh no. She sang Let It Go like eleven times before lunch and the microphone makes echo noises. Dad said he regrets nothing. Mom said he will.
entries.highlight: Got Mario Kart and a flame bike helmet for Christmas while Tessa sang endlessly on her new karaoke machine.

entries.title: Winter break at Jack's
entries.body: No school because of winter break so I went to Jack's house all day. Jack got Mario Kart too, so we had a race to see who unlocked more stuff. Jack's dog Pepper kept sitting on the controller cord. We also went outside and did a snowball fight with Jack's big sister and she was too good. She hit me right in the ear. I was cold but it was still so fun.
entries.highlight: Spent a winter break day at Jack's racing Mario Kart and having a snowball fight.

entries.title: New Year's room cleanup
entries.body: It is a new year! Mom said a new year means a clean room. That is not a real rule. I had to clean my room and I found three missing socks again, which means my socks run away under my bed every month. I also found a Christmas candy cane in my backpack. I ate it. Mom said I should do a New Year resolution. Mine is to beat Jafie at Pokemon. She said that is not what it means.
entries.highlight: Cleaned his room on New Year's Day and made a resolution to beat Jafie at Pokemon.

entries.title: Blue team at Mateo's party
entries.body: I went to Mateo's birthday party at the laser tag place. Mateo turned nine. We were on teams, red against blue, and I was blue. I got tagged a lot at the start because my vest kept beeping. But then I hid behind the big wall and got like fifteen people. Our team lost by a tiny bit and I said the red team had more grown ups, which is unfair. Then we had pizza and cake and I forgot about it.
entries.highlight: Played laser tag at Mateo's ninth birthday party and complained a little when his team lost.

entries.title: French toast at Jafie's sleepover
entries.body: Last night I slept over at Jafie's house. It was the last night of winter break. We stayed up until eleven telling scary stories with a flashlight. Jafie's story was about a ghost who lives in a vending machine and honestly it was not scary at all. This morning his mom made French toast with whipped cream shaped like a smiley face. I had two. I am so tired now but it was worth it.
entries.highlight: Slept over at Jafie's house, told flashlight stories and had French toast for breakfast.

entries.title: Freezing fishing with Dad
entries.body: Dad took me fishing at the lake after school even though it was so cold. He wanted to try his new reel. We wore our big hats and sat on buckets. We had sandwiches and hot chocolate in a thermos. We did not catch anything, not even a little one. Dad says there is a giant catfish in the lake named Big Gary. He has never seen him. I think Big Gary is made up.
entries.highlight: Went cold-weather fishing with Dad, caught nothing, and heard the legend of Big Gary the catfish.

entries.title: Tessa sang outside my door
entries.body: My sister was so annoying today. Tessa took her karaoke machine and sang outside my door while I was doing homework. She sang the same song over and over and the echo button was on. I told her to stop and she said it is a free country. She does not even know what that means. Then she threw a fit when Mom took the microphone. I kind of felt bad. Kind of.
entries.highlight: Got annoyed when Tessa sang karaoke outside his door during homework.

entries.title: Owen's basement sleepover
entries.body: Last night I slept over at Owen's house in his basement. We had a movie night and watched a movie about a dog who plays football. We made popcorn and Owen spilled half of it on the Lego city. We tried to stay up all night but Owen fell asleep at like ten thirty. I stayed up until eleven so I won. Then his brother scared us in the morning by growling. I screamed a little.
entries.highlight: Had a movie-night sleepover at Owen's and was proud to stay up the latest.

entries.title: My ninth birthday sleepover
entries.body: My birthday sleepover! I am nine now. Jack, Jafie, Mateo, Owen and Eli all came, so five friends. We had two pizzas. I said we needed a hundred but Mom said two. We had a Mario Kart tournament and I made it to the final but Jack beat me on Rainbow Road. I got so mad I went in the bathroom for a minute. Then I came out and we had cake and it was okay again.
entries.highlight: Turned nine with a five-friend sleepover and Mario Kart tournament, getting upset after losing the final.

entries.title: Setting up for the big night
entries.body: I forgot to say about this morning. Dad made chocolate chip pancakes with a nine made out of whipped cream. Tessa gave me a card she made and it said happy birthday Andy with a picture of me as a dinosaur. It is kind of good actually. Then me and Mom set up six sleeping bags in the living room in a circle. I made a sign for the tournament that said ANDY'S BIRTHDAY CUP. I was so excited I could not sit still.
entries.highlight: Spent his birthday morning with family and set up the living room for his sleepover.

entries.title: No school fishing day
entries.body: No school today because it is Martin Luther King Day. So Dad and me went back to the lake. We had salami sandwiches and chips. I caught a little sunfish! It was smaller than my hand but it still counts. Dad took a picture and then we let it go. Dad said maybe it is Big Gary's grandkid. I said Big Gary is fake and Dad said that is what Big Gary wants me to think.
entries.favorite: Catching my first fish of the year
entries.highlight: Caught a small sunfish on a fishing trip with Dad during the school holiday.

entries.title: Fit at the grocery store
entries.body: My sister was so annoying today. We went to the grocery store and Tessa threw a fit because Mom said no to the cereal with the mermaid on it. She lay down on the floor in the cereal aisle. A lady looked at us. I pretended I did not know her. Then Mom let me pick a cereal and I picked the chocolate one and Tessa cried even more. Maybe I should have picked the mermaid one.
entries.highlight: Watched Tessa throw a fit at the grocery store and wondered if he should have chosen differently.

entries.title: The blue shell ruined everything
entries.body: Mateo came over and we played Mario Kart. He beat me on every single track, like eight in a row. On the last one a blue shell hit me right before the finish line and I came in fourth. I yelled that the game is rigged and I threw my controller on the couch. Mateo said dude, calm down. I sat on the stairs for a while and did not want to play anymore. Mom said winning is fun but being a sore loser is not. We played Legos after and that was better.
entries.highlight: Got very upset after losing every Mario Kart race to Mateo and needed time to cool down.

entries.title: Socks and a lost Pokemon card
entries.body: I had to clean my room again. It took forever. Under my bed there was a whole sock family AND a Pokemon card I thought Tessa stole. So she did not steal it. I did not tell her that. I also put my clothes in the drawers instead of on the floor, which Mom said was a miracle. Mom gave me a sticker on the chore chart. Five more stickers and I get a booster pack.
entries.highlight: Cleaned his room, found a card he blamed Tessa for taking, and earned a chore chart sticker.

entries.title: Lunch table card battles
entries.body: At lunch today we battled Pokemon with our cards. We are only allowed if we finish eating first. Jack beat me in the first game because he had a Mewtwo. Then I beat Jafie because his deck only had two energy cards. The lunch lady said we were too loud and she took away the cards until recess. Mr. Dawson gave them back. He said he used to play too.
entries.favorite: Mr. Dawson used to play too
entries.highlight: Battled Pokemon cards with friends at lunch and learned his teacher used to play.

entries.title: Owen's brother's old Game Boy
entries.body: I went to Owen's house after school. His brother let us play his really old Game Boy. The screen is green and tiny and the games are super hard. We played a Pokemon game from like before I was born. Owen's mom said she played it when she was a kid. That is crazy. Then we went down to the Lego city and built an airport. Owen made the runway out of gray pieces.
entries.highlight: Played an old Game Boy at Owen's house and built a Lego airport together.

entries.title: Valentine pancakes before school
entries.body: Dad made chocolate pancakes this morning before school because tomorrow is Valentine's Day and he will be at work early. He made one in a heart shape. Tessa did not throw a fit at all, which is a record. I ate three. Then I had to brush my teeth super fast because carpool was honking. I still had chocolate on my chin at school and Jafie told me. Embarrassing.
entries.highlight: Dad made early chocolate pancakes for Valentine's week, and Tessa stayed calm at breakfast.

entries.title: Board game Sunday instead
entries.body: Mom said no video games today because I played too much over the weekend. I said that is like a punishment and she said it is called a Sunday. So we played a board game with the whole family, the one where you build roads and trade sheep. Dad kept trading sheep with Tessa because she does not know what they are worth. I won! I got the longest road. I still wanted to play games though.
entries.highlight: Played a family board game during a no-screens Sunday and won.

entries.title: Minecraft castle on Presidents Day
entries.body: There was no school today because of Presidents Day. I played Minecraft for like six hours straight. Not really, like two hours, Mom has a timer. I built a castle with a moat and lava around it and a secret room under the throne. A creeper blew up the side of it and I yelled so loud. Mom asked what happened. I said a creeper. She did not know what that is.
entries.highlight: Built a Minecraft castle on a school holiday and was annoyed when a creeper blew part of it up.

entries.title: I quit Smash and Eli went home
entries.body: Eli came over and we played Smash Brothers. Eli is so good with Kirby. He beat me five times in a row. On the sixth time I lost again and I got so mad I unplugged the Switch. Eli said why did you do that and I said because it is my Switch. He called his mom to pick him up. Now I feel bad. Mom said I need to learn to lose, and that a game is just a game.
entries.highlight: Unplugged the game after losing at Smash, and Eli went home early; Mom talked to him about losing well.

entries.title: Dad lost a fish and laughed
entries.body: Fishing again with Dad. I caught nothing but Dad hooked a big one! It pulled so hard his pole bent all the way. Then the line snapped and it got away. I thought Dad would be mad but he just laughed and said that was Big Gary saying hi. I would have been so mad if it was me. Dad said you cannot catch them all. That is a Pokemon thing though.
entries.highlight: Watched Dad lose a big fish and laugh it off, which surprised him.

entries.title: Wing eating contest with Dad
entries.body: We had chicken wings for dinner. Mom got the honey barbecue kind and the spicy kind. I had seven barbecue ones and Dad had like twelve. We had a contest and Dad won but I think he cheated because he has a bigger mouth. I tried one spicy one and my tongue was on fire and I drank a whole glass of milk. Tessa only ate the celery. Weird.
entries.highlight: Had a wing-eating contest with Dad and tried a spicy wing for the first time.

entries.title: Dad teaches me Magic
entries.body: Dad taught me how to play Magic the Gathering. It is his card game from when he was a kid and he has boxes and boxes of cards. It is way harder than Pokemon. There is mana and creatures and tapping, which means turning your card sideways. Dad has a dragon deck. I played with his green elf deck. I lost two times but I almost won the second time. Dad said I learn fast.
entries.highlight: Learned to play Magic the Gathering with Dad and almost won his second game.

entries.title: The blanket hideout with Tessa
entries.body: My sister was so annoying this morning. Tessa kept knocking on my door every two minutes asking if I wanted to play. I said no like ten times. Then it started raining and there was nothing to do, so we built a hideout in her room with her pink blanket and my dinosaur blanket. She brought snacks in, which was actually a good idea. We played that the hideout was a spaceship and she was the alien. It was kind of fun. Don't tell her.
entries.highlight: Built a blanket hideout with Tessa on a rainy day and secretly had fun playing with her.

entries.title: My deck finally beat Jack's Mewtwo
entries.body: At lunch we battled Pokemon with our cards again. I changed my deck so it has more fighting types because Mewtwo is weak to dark, no wait, that is the new one. Anyway I asked Mateo and he helped. Jack played his Mewtwo and I knocked it out with my Umbreon! Everybody at the table went ohhhh. Jack said rematch tomorrow. I was so happy I forgot to eat my apple.
entries.highlight: Rebuilt his Pokemon deck with Mateo's help and beat Jack's Mewtwo at lunch.

entries.title: No school Pokemon marathon
entries.body: There was no school today because of teacher conferences. Mom and Dad went to talk to Mr. Dawson and I stayed with Grandma. I played Pokemon for like six hours straight. Not really, Grandma does not know about the timer so maybe three hours. I caught a shiny Eevee! Mom and Dad came back and said Mr. Dawson says I am smart but I rush. I do not rush. I just go fast.
entries.highlight: Played Pokemon at Grandma's on a conference day and heard his teacher says he rushes.

entries.title: The rushing problem
entries.body: I had so much homework today. A math page with twenty problems and a reading log. Because of what Mr. Dawson said, Mom made me check every problem after I finished. I found two mistakes. I did not tell her I found them. Okay, I did tell her. She said see, slowing down works. I finished it all before dinner and then I wore green for St. Patrick's Day so nobody could pinch me.
entries.highlight: Started checking his math work after a teacher's comment and caught two mistakes.

entries.title: Evening worms with Dad
entries.body: After dinner me and Dad went down to the lake for like an hour before it got dark. We used worms this time instead of the shiny lure. I had to put the worm on the hook myself. It was so squishy and gross but I did it. We caught nothing again. Dad said fishing is not about the fish. I said then why is it called fishing. He laughed so hard he almost fell off the bucket.
entries.highlight: Baited his own hook for the first time on an evening fishing trip with Dad.

entries.title: I said good game to Eli
entries.body: Eli came over and we played Smash Brothers for the first time since I unplugged the Switch. Before he came Mom said remember what we talked about. Eli beat me three times. I really wanted to throw the controller but I didn't. I said good game. It felt weird to say it. Then I beat him once with Link and Eli said good game too. We played until his mom came and nobody got mad.
entries.highlight: Lost to Eli at Smash Brothers and said good game instead of getting angry, for the first time.

entries.title: Recess basketball with Jafie
entries.body: At recess me and Jafie played basketball on the blacktop. The hoop has no net so it is hard to tell if it went in. We played to eleven. Jafie is shorter than me but he is really fast at stealing. I won eleven to nine. I did not brag that much. Just a little. Then the bell rang and we raced to the line and Jafie won that, so we are even.
entries.highlight: Played recess basketball with Jafie and won, then lost a race back to class.

entries.title: Jack's new basketball shoes
entries.body: Me and Jack played basketball at the park after school. Jack got new shoes that are bright orange and he said they make him jump higher. They do not. We played one on one and he won by two. He said it was the shoes. I said it was luck. Then we just shot from far away and I made one from the line by the bench. Jack said that was luck. Ha.
entries.highlight: Played one-on-one basketball with Jack and they teased each other about luck.

entries.title: Screen-free Sunday treasure hunt
entries.body: Mom said no video games today. It is screen free Sunday now, like every Sunday. That is so many Sundays. I was bored so I made a treasure hunt for Tessa with clues around the yard. The treasure was two of my old Pokemon cards and a bouncy ball. She could not read the clues so I had to read them to her, which kind of ruins it. But she screamed when she found it. It was a good scream.
entries.favorite: Tessa screaming when she found it
entries.highlight: Made a backyard treasure hunt for Tessa on the family's new screen-free Sundays.

entries.title: Jafie's dad grills in March
entries.body: I went to Jafie's house after school. His dad was grilling hot dogs in the backyard even though it was kind of chilly. Jafie has a trampoline with a net and we played a game where you try to knock the other person down with a big ball. I knocked him down four times and he knocked me down five. Then we ate the hot dogs on the trampoline and bounced a little. A hot dog fell through the springs.
entries.favorite: Eating hot dogs on the trampoline
entries.highlight: Played on Jafie's trampoline and ate grilled hot dogs at his house after school.

entries.title: Owen's granny shot
entries.body: Me and Owen played basketball at the park. Owen shoots like a granny, with two hands from between his legs. But it goes in a lot! I tried it and it went over the whole backboard. We were laughing so hard. Then some big kids came and we had to share the court. One of them showed us how to do a bounce pass the right way. He was like in high school. He was so tall.
entries.highlight: Played basketball with Owen, laughed at his unusual shot, and got tips from an older kid.

entries.title: Minivan to the bowling alley
entries.body: Jack's mom drove a bunch of us to the bowling alley in her minivan, so it was like carpool but on a Sunday. Everybody was singing really loud to the radio. Owen sat in the very back and said he did not feel good, so we opened the windows. Nobody puked. At bowling I got a strike in the first frame and then like four gutter balls. Jack had the bumpers up and said he did not.
entries.favorite: My strike in the first frame
entries.highlight: Rode with friends to go bowling and got a strike in the first frame.

entries.title: Scooter at the skate park
entries.body: I tried the skate park on my scooter after school for the first time. There are big ramps and bowls and teenagers do flips. I just rode on the flat part mostly. Then I tried a little ramp and I fell and my knee got scraped and it bled a lot. I did not cry. Well, a little bit in the car. Mom put a big bandage on it. It was April Fools Day so I told Tessa my leg fell off.
entries.highlight: Tried the skate park on his scooter for the first time and scraped his knee.

entries.title: Mario Kart Friday
entries.body: Friday means bonus Mario Kart, because Mom gives me an extra hour on Fridays. I used every single minute. I unlocked the gold glider finally. I also played online against people from other countries. One guy was from Japan. I came in second against him. Second place in the whole world. Okay, in that one race. Then Mom said screens off, shoes on, and we went for a walk.
entries.highlight: Earned a Friday bonus hour of Mario Kart and unlocked a new item.

entries.title: Game Haven trade day
entries.body: Dad took me to Game Haven for the Sunday trade day. People put their cards on the tables and you can trade. I traded two doubles for a Lucario that has a cool shiny border. The guy at the counter, his name is Dale, said it was a fair trade. I asked him like four times to be sure. Then I battled a kid who was seven and I let him win one. Not really, he was good.
entries.highlight: Made a fair trade for a Lucario card at the card shop and battled a younger kid.

entries.title: Rain day without screens
entries.body: Mom said no video games today because I did not finish my reading log yesterday. It was actually not that bad. It rained so I read my book about a kid who gets stuck in a video game, which is kind of ironic. That is a word Mr. Dawson taught us. I read three chapters. Then I drew a map of the world from the book. I am gonna show Jack tomorrow.
entries.favorite: Drawing the map from my book
entries.highlight: Lost screen time for a missed reading log, then read three chapters and drew a map.

entries.title: Long homework and a timer
entries.body: I had so much homework today. We are doing fractions and they make no sense. Like why is one half bigger than one fourth when four is bigger than two? Mom drew pizzas to explain it. Then it made sense. I asked to play Mario Kart first and she said homework first, the rule is the rule. I was mad for ten minutes. I finished it all before dinner and played after.
entries.highlight: Struggled with fractions until Mom explained them with pizzas, and argued about the homework-first rule.

entries.title: My first goal of the season
entries.body: I had a soccer game this morning. Our team is the Thunder and our shirts are yellow. I scored a goal! It went right between the goalie's legs. I did a slide on the grass to celebrate and got a grass stain. We lost four to three though. Coach Mike said I played great. I was mad we lost but Mom said I could be happy about my goal and sad about the game at the same time.
entries.highlight: Scored a goal in his soccer game even though his team lost four to three.

entries.title: First time at the pump track
entries.body: This morning was Easter and I found nineteen eggs. Tessa found eleven. Then in the afternoon Dad took me to the pump track for the first time. It is like a skate park made of dirt for bikes. You go over the bumps without pedaling by pushing your bike down. There is a giant jump at the end that the big kids call the Monster. I did not try it. I just looked at it. It is so tall.
entries.highlight: Visited the pump track for the first time on Easter and was too nervous to try the big jump.

entries.title: Easter night Magic duel
entries.body: After Easter dinner Dad and me played Magic the Gathering on the living room floor. I am getting better. I know what tapping is and what flying means now. Dad played his big red dragon and I had nothing to stop it. But I made him use almost all his life points first. I mean life, not life points. Dad says I am really close to winning. I think next time.
entries.highlight: Played Magic with Dad after Easter dinner and felt close to winning.

entries.title: The Charizard trade fight
entries.body: At lunch me and Jack had a really big fight. Yesterday I traded him my Charizard for two of his cards. Today I said I wanted a trade back because I found out his cards were not as good. Jack said no trade backs. I said he tricked me. He said I am a baby. I said he is a cheater. Now we are not talking. I sat with Mateo at the end of lunch. My stomach feels weird.
entries.highlight: Had a big fight with Jack over a Pokemon card trade and they stopped talking.

entries.title: Riding with Mateo instead of Jack
entries.body: Me and Mateo rode bikes around the neighborhood after school. Usually it is me and Jack but we are still not talking. Mateo has a new bike with gears. We rode to the end of the street and around the pond and back. My flame helmet looks so cool. Mateo asked if I was still mad at Jack. I said maybe. He said Jack is sad too. I did not know that.
entries.highlight: Biked with Mateo while still fighting with Jack, and learned Jack was sad too.

entries.title: Racing alone after the bike ride
entries.body: After my homework I played a racing game for like six hours straight. Not really, Mom's timer is forty five minutes on school nights. It is the new car one where you can paint your car. I painted mine red with flames like my helmet. I won the cup on hard mode. I usually play this one with Jack. It was kind of boring by myself. I kind of miss him.
entries.highlight: Played a racing game alone after homework and realized he missed playing with Jack.

entries.title: Owen puked in carpool
entries.body: In carpool today everybody was singing really loud like always, except me and Jack, because we were still not talking. Then Owen said his stomach hurt and he puked! In the car! It got on his backpack and a little on Mateo's shoe. Jack's mom pulled over and everybody screamed. Me and Jack looked at each other and almost laughed. It was the first time we looked at each other all week.
entries.highlight: Owen got carsick in carpool, and the chaos made Andy and Jack almost laugh together during their fight.

entries.title: Friday night soccer under lights
entries.body: I had a soccer game tonight at the big field with the lights. I scored a goal! It was a header, which I have never done before. My head hurt a little. We lost again, two to one. Coach Mike says we are getting better. I wanted to kick the ball really far after the game because I was mad but I didn't. I high fived the other team in the line. Some of them were sweaty.
entries.highlight: Scored his first header goal in a Friday night soccer game and high-fived the other team after losing.

entries.title: Talking about Jack while fishing
entries.body: On Sunday we went fishing, just me and Dad. We had turkey sandwiches and pretzels. I caught a bass that was like this big, as big as my shoe! While we waited for fish I told Dad about the fight with Jack. Dad said sometimes when you are really mad you say stuff you do not mean. He said the hard part is saying sorry first. I think I have to say sorry first. Ugh.
entries.highlight: Caught a bass with Dad and talked through his fight with Jack, deciding to apologize.

entries.title: Back at the skate park ramp
entries.body: I went back to the skate park on my scooter after school. My knee is almost healed, it just has a pink spot. I went down the little ramp three times without falling! The fourth time I fell but on my butt, so it did not hurt. A teenager with blue hair said nice one, little dude. I am not little. But it was still nice. I want to try the medium ramp next time.
entries.highlight: Went back to the skate park and rode the small ramp three times without falling.

entries.title: Owen says just talk to him
entries.body: Owen and me shot hoops at the park. He is totally better from puking. He said you have to just talk to Jack because it is weird at lunch now. He said the whole table is sad. I said I know. Then we played around the world and Owen beat me. He did the granny shot from the far spot and it went in and he danced. I am gonna talk to Jack next week.
entries.highlight: Played basketball with Owen, who encouraged him to make up with Jack.

entries.title: Eli taught me a spin move
entries.body: Me and Eli played basketball at the park on Saturday morning. Eli's dad taught him a spin move and Eli taught it to me. You dribble then you turn around really fast. The first time I tried it I spun and the ball rolled away into the grass. By the tenth time I could kind of do it. We played two games and we each won one. That is fair. Eli brought Biscuit and she chased the ball.
entries.highlight: Learned a basketball spin move from Eli and split two games with him.

entries.title: Building my first Magic deck
entries.body: Dad taught me how to build my own Magic the Gathering deck tonight after homework. You need sixty cards and the right amount of lands. I picked green because green has big animals and elves. My best card is a giant bear. Dad says I have to think about what my opponent will do, not just what I want to do. That is a lot of thinking. We play the new deck this weekend.
entries.highlight: Built his first Magic deck with Dad, choosing green creatures.

entries.title: I said sorry first
entries.body: In carpool today I said sorry to Jack. I said it really fast before I could change my mind. I said sorry I called you a cheater, the trade was fair. Jack said sorry I called you a baby. Then everybody in the car went awww and we both said shut up. Then we sang really loud with everybody. Nobody puked this time. It was the best carpool ever.
entries.highlight: Apologized to Jack in carpool, ending their fight over the card trade.

entries.title: Jafie's pool noodle party
entries.body: I went to Jafie's birthday party. He is nine now too. It was at the indoor pool at the rec center because it is still too cold outside. We had a pool noodle fight and Jack was on my team, like normal again. We beat Mateo and Owen. Then we had cake that was blue and our tongues turned blue. I ate three pieces. Jafie got a new Pokemon game. I am so jealous.
entries.highlight: Went to Jafie's ninth birthday at an indoor pool and teamed up with Jack again after making up.

entries.title: Jack gave the Charizard back
entries.body: At lunch we battled Pokemon with our cards. Then Jack did something crazy. He gave me back my Charizard! He said it was never fun having it because of the fight. I gave him back his two cards too. Then we made a rule with the whole table. No trade backs, but you have to wait one day before a trade counts. Mateo wrote it on a napkin. It is official now.
entries.highlight: Got his Charizard back from Jack, and the lunch table made a fair-trading rule together.

entries.title: Mateo's bike gears
entries.body: After school Mateo and me rode around the block again. Mateo let me try his bike with gears. It is so weird, you click the handle and it gets harder or easier. I went up the big hill on Cedar Street on the easy gear and did not even have to stand up. On my bike I always have to walk up that hill. I am asking for gears for my birthday. Or Christmas. Whichever comes first.
entries.highlight: Tried Mateo's geared bike and rode up a big hill without stopping.

entries.title: Two player Mario Kart cups
entries.body: Mateo came over and we played Mario Kart. We did the team mode where you are on the same team against the computers. We won the Mushroom Cup and the Flower Cup. Then we raced each other and Mateo beat me in the last race by like one second. I said good game, Mateo. He looked at me funny because last time I threw my controller. I said I am different now. He laughed.
entries.highlight: Played Mario Kart with Mateo and said good game after losing, unlike last time.

entries.title: Pizza night with extra pepperoni
entries.body: We had pizza for dinner. It is Friday pizza night. Dad got pepperoni with extra pepperoni, which means there is a bajillion on it. I counted on my slice and there were nineteen. Tessa picks hers off and gives them to me, so I had twenty five. Then we watched a movie on the couch. Mom fell asleep in the middle. It was so good.
entries.highlight: Enjoyed family pizza night and counted the pepperonis on his slice.

entries.title: Small tournament at Game Haven
entries.body: Dad took me to a small Pokemon card tournament at Game Haven. There were twelve kids. I won my first game and lost the second and won the third. I came in fourth! I got a promo card for playing. One kid cried when he lost to me and I did not know what to do. I said good game and he said thanks. Dale said that was the right thing.
entries.highlight: Placed fourth in a small Pokemon card tournament and said good game to a kid who was upset.

entries.title: Cannonball day at Jack's
entries.body: I went to Jack's house on Sunday. It was finally hot enough to go in his pool. The water was still freezing though. We did cannonballs off the side and Jack's mom gave us scores like the Olympics. I got a nine. Jack got an eight point five. He said she is biased toward me because I am the guest. Then we made root beer floats. School ends this week!
entries.favorite: Getting a nine on my cannonball
entries.highlight: Swam in Jack's backyard pool on the first hot weekend and made root beer floats.

entries.title: Last lunch battles of third grade
entries.body: At lunch we battled Pokemon with our cards. It is the last week of school so Mr. Dawson let us play in the classroom after lunch too. Jafie brought his whole binder. I beat Jafie and Owen and lost to Jack. I said good game and I meant it. We are gonna battle all summer at Game Haven. Mr. Dawson showed us his old Blastoise from when he was a kid.
entries.highlight: Played Pokemon cards in class during the last week of school and said good game after losing.

entries.title: Room cleaning for summer
entries.body: I had to clean my room. It took forever. Mom said you cannot start summer with a messy room. I found my winter gloves and a Valentine card from school and a pencil that was chewed. Probably by me. I put all my school papers in a box. There were so many math sheets. I kept my good spelling test with the star and threw out the rest. Summer is almost here!
entries.highlight: Cleaned his room before summer and sorted his school papers.

entries.title: Last day of third grade
entries.body: Last day of school! No more homework for the whole summer. Mr. Dawson gave everybody an award and mine was Most Likely to Make the Class Laugh. Jack got Best Basketball Player. We signed each other's shirts with markers. I am gonna miss Mr. Dawson a little because he let us play cards. Summer plan is pump track every day, Pokemon every day, and sleepovers every weekend. Mom said we will see.
entries.highlight: Finished third grade with a class award for making people laugh and big summer plans.

entries.title: Celebration booster pack
entries.body: After school Dad took me to Game Haven to celebrate summer. He let me pick two booster packs because I got a good report card, all Bs and one A in reading. In the second pack I got a full art Gardevoir! Dale said that is worth like twenty dollars. I am never selling it. Then we got slushies next door. Mine was blue raspberry and my tongue is still blue.
entries.highlight: Celebrated a good report card with booster packs from Dad and pulled a rare card.

entries.title: Card battles at day camp
entries.body: This week I started day camp at the rec center. It is like school but you play games and go swimming. At lunch some kids battled Pokemon with their cards. I brought my deck and I beat a kid named Diego two times. He is ten and he was surprised. I showed everybody my Gardevoir and a counselor said put it away before it gets ketchup on it. Good idea.
entries.highlight: Started summer day camp and won Pokemon card battles against an older camper.

entries.title: Hot day hoops with Eli
entries.body: After camp me and Eli went to the courts. It was so hot the court felt like lava. I did Eli's spin move and it worked and I scored! Eli said I learned it better than him. We played to fifteen and I won fifteen to twelve. Then we got popsicles from the ice cream truck. Mine was the one shaped like a cartoon face and its eyes were gum balls.
entries.highlight: Used the spin move Eli taught him and won a hot summer basketball game.

entries.title: Pancakes and a tower of four
entries.body: Dad made chocolate pancakes for Saturday breakfast. I ate four, which is my new record. I stacked them into a tower and put whipped cream on top like a snowy mountain. Tessa wanted a tower too, so I made hers. She only ate one pancake and then said she was full. Then Dad ate the rest of her tower. That is the deal at our house, if you do not finish, Dad gets it.
entries.highlight: Ate a record four chocolate pancakes and built Tessa her own pancake tower.

entries.title: Pump track practice with Eli
entries.body: Me and Eli rode bikes to the pump track. Eli is really good there because his cousin taught him. I did the whole small loop without pedaling three times in a row. Then I tried the medium bumps and I got air! Like a little bit. Eli said maybe two inches. I looked at the Monster again. It is still so tall. Eli did it and landed it. I said maybe next week. Maybe.
entries.favorite: Getting a little bit of air
entries.highlight: Practiced at the pump track with Eli, got some air on medium bumps, and looked at the big jump.

entries.title: Dropping in at the skate park
entries.body: I went to the skate park on my scooter and I dropped in on the medium ramp! Dropping in means you start at the very top and go straight down. My legs were shaking. I stood there for like five minutes. A teenager said just lean forward. I did it and I did not fall. I did it four more times. Last time in April I fell on the little ramp. Now look.
entries.favorite: Dropping in for the first time
entries.highlight: Dropped in on the medium ramp at the skate park after months of practice.

entries.title: Summer league soccer goal
entries.body: I had a summer soccer game tonight. Summer league is mixed up teams so Mateo is on my team now. I scored a goal! Mateo passed it to me and I kicked it in the corner. We lost three to two though, again. I said good game to the other team and did not even want to say anything mean. Mateo said our team is like the Thunder all over again. True.
entries.highlight: Scored a goal off Mateo's pass in summer soccer and stayed a good sport after losing.

entries.title: Owen's training ride
entries.body: Me and Owen rode bikes around the neighborhood on Sunday. Owen is not that good at bikes, he still wobbles. So I showed him how to stand up on the pedals going over bumps, like at the pump track. We practiced on the curb ramps on our street. By the end he did it without wobbling. He said I am a good teacher. I never taught anybody anything before. It felt kind of cool.
entries.highlight: Taught Owen to ride over bumps on his bike and felt proud being a teacher.

entries.title: Cleaning before the cousins came
entries.body: I had to clean my room because my cousins came over for Fourth of July. It took forever. I found a sock that was so old it was stiff. I hid my best cards in my closet so my cousin Benny would not touch them. He is four and he licks things. Then we had hamburgers and watched the fireworks from the hill by the school. The big gold ones were the best. Tessa covered her ears the whole time.
entries.highlight: Cleaned his room for the family Fourth of July party and watched fireworks with cousins.

entries.title: Hideout Captain Tessa
entries.body: My sister was annoying this morning because she kept singing on her karaoke machine at seven. But then we built the biggest hideout ever in the living room with every blanket in the house and the card table. It had two rooms and a tunnel. I let Tessa be the captain of the hideout, even though I built most of it. She made rules like no grumpy people allowed. We ate lunch in there. Mom took a picture of us.
entries.highlight: Built a giant two-room hideout with Tessa and let her be the captain.

entries.title: Diego's trade offer at camp
entries.body: At camp lunch Diego wanted to trade me for my Gardevoir. He offered five cards. I almost said yes, but then I remembered the napkin rule and said I will think about it until tomorrow. At home I looked them up with Dad and Diego's cards were all common ones. So I said no thanks. Diego said okay. The napkin rule works even at camp. Mateo would be proud, he is the one who wrote it down. I put the Gardevoir back in the front of my binder where it belongs.
entries.highlight: Waited a day before a card trade, as his friends' rule said, and turned down an unfair offer.

entries.title: Rolling the Monster
entries.body: Me and Owen rode to the pump track. Owen just did the small loop because he is still learning. I rolled over the Monster really slow without jumping, just to see what it feels like. It is so steep on the other side. My stomach dropped like on a rollercoaster. But I did it. Owen cheered. Next I have to go fast enough to actually jump it. Eli says go on Sunday when he is there.
entries.highlight: Rolled slowly over the big pump track jump for the first time to get used to it.

entries.title: Dad's lucky green lure
entries.body: Dad took me fishing at the lake on Monday because he took the day off work. I caught three bluegills on his lucky green lure! Dad caught one. Ha, I beat Dad. We had ham sandwiches and those little orange crackers. Dad said Big Gary probably heard about me and is hiding. I told him about the Monster jump and he said I should only do it when I am ready, not because someone says so.
entries.highlight: Out-fished Dad with three bluegills and talked with him about the scary pump track jump.

entries.title: Jack's summer growth spurt
entries.body: Jack and me went to the park to shoot hoops. Jack grew like a whole inch this summer and it is not fair. He can almost touch the net now. We played one on one and he beat me twice. I said good game but I also said you are a giraffe now. He laughed. Then we lay on the grass and talked about fourth grade. We both hope we get the same teacher.
entries.highlight: Played basketball with a taller Jack and talked about hoping to share a fourth-grade class.

entries.title: Owen's backyard pool party
entries.body: I went to Owen's birthday party. He turned nine and it was a pool party in his backyard. They have a slide that goes into the pool! We did chicken fights and I was on Jack's shoulders and we won every time. Owen's brother made a giant water balloon fight and I got hit in the face. Then cake. It was a Lego cake. I told everybody I am doing the Monster jump tomorrow.
entries.highlight: Celebrated Owen's ninth birthday at a backyard pool party and announced his plan to try the big jump.

entries.title: I landed the Monster
entries.body: I did it. I did the biggest jump at the pump track and I landed it! The Monster! I was so scared at the top that my hands were sweating on the handlebars. Eli said just pump the last two bumps hard and look at where you want to land. I went and I flew and I landed on both wheels. Eli filmed it on his mom's phone. I watched it like twenty times. In April I could not even look at it.
entries.highlight: Landed the biggest jump at the pump track for the first time while Eli filmed, after months of practice.

entries.title: Taco night victory dinner
entries.body: We had tacos for dinner because Mom said it was a celebration dinner for the Monster jump. I got to pick so I picked tacos with the hard shells. I had four and one of them broke into a million pieces. Dad watched Eli's video again and said I looked like a pro. Tessa said she wants to jump the Monster too. She is five and she has training wheels. Honestly, it was a really good dinner.
entries.highlight: Had a family taco dinner celebrating his big jump, and Tessa wanted to try it too.

entries.title: Camp carpool karaoke
entries.body: In carpool to camp everybody was singing really loud. Jack's mom drives us in summer too. Jack tried to sing the high part and sounded like a squeaky door. Then Mateo made up new words about Owen puking and Owen said that is not funny but he was laughing. Nobody puked this time, which we say every time now. Then Jack's mom made us listen to her music. It was old.
entries.highlight: Sang in the summer camp carpool, where joking about Owen getting carsick has become a running gag.

entries.title: The one that got away again
entries.body: Dad took me fishing at the lake early in the morning when it was foggy. Something big grabbed my line and pulled so hard I almost dropped the pole. Dad helped me hold it and we reeled for like a minute. Then it jumped and spit out the hook. It was huge, like as long as my arm. Dad said that was Big Gary for sure. Okay, maybe Big Gary is real. I was so mad but also kind of happy I saw him.
entries.highlight: Hooked and lost a very large fish with Dad, starting to believe in Big Gary.

entries.title: Rainy day racing marathon
entries.body: It rained all day so there was no pump track and no camp pool. So I played the racing game basically all day. Okay, two and a half hours with breaks, because Mom made me eat lunch and walk around the block. I finally beat the hardest championship on expert mode. Then I painted a new car to look like the Monster jump with dirt brown and green stripes. It looks kind of ugly but I love it.
entries.highlight: Beat a racing game championship on expert mode during a rainy summer day.

entries.title: Library day without screens
entries.body: Mom said no video games today because I was on the Switch too much this week. It was actually not that bad. We went to the library and I found a graphic novel about a kid who rides BMX bikes. I read the whole thing on the beanbag in the kids part. Then I got two more. Tessa got a book about a pig who goes to the moon. I read it to her at bedtime. She made me read it twice.
entries.highlight: Spent a no-screens day reading graphic novels at the library and read a bedtime story to Tessa.

entries.title: I beat Dad at Magic
entries.body: Dad and me played Magic the Gathering after dinner and I beat Dad! For real, he did not let me. I played my elf that makes extra mana and then my giant bear and then another bear and he could not stop them. Dad's dragon came out too late. Dad said good game and shook my hand like a real tournament. I said good game too. Then I did a little dance. Just a little one.
entries.highlight: Won his first game of Magic against Dad, and they shook hands like a real tournament.

entries.title: Owen tried the medium bumps
entries.body: Me and Owen rode bikes around the neighborhood and then went to the pump track. Owen did the medium bumps for the first time because I showed him how to pump with his arms. He got a little air and yelled so loud. I did the Monster two times and landed it both times. It does not even feel scary now. Well, a tiny bit. Owen said he wants to do it before school starts.
entries.favorite: Owen yelling on the medium bumps
entries.highlight: Helped Owen try the medium pump track bumps and landed the big jump twice more.

entries.title: Tessa is scared of kindergarten
entries.body: My sister was kind of annoying today because she would not stop crying about kindergarten. She starts in two weeks and she is scared that nobody will play with her. She threw a fit about her new backpack because it was the wrong purple. Then at night I told her that kindergarten is the best grade because you get to nap and play blocks. She stopped crying. I did not tell her the nap part might not be true.
entries.highlight: Comforted Tessa when she got upset about starting kindergarten.

entries.title: Last camp card battles
entries.body: It was the last week of day camp, so at lunch we did a big Pokemon card battle with everybody who brought decks. There were like nine kids. I won three games and lost two. Diego won the most. I told him good game and he gave me one of his extra energy cards. He is not that bad. I will miss camp a little bit but not the swim test.
entries.favorite: Getting an energy card from Diego
entries.highlight: Played in a last-week camp card battle and ended on good terms with Diego.

entries.title: Mateo's new puppy
entries.body: After camp I went to Mateo's house. Mateo got a puppy! Her name is Noodle because she is long and skinny. She is a wiener dog. She bit my shoelaces and would not let go. We tried to teach her sit and she just rolled over, which is not the same thing. Mateo's mom said Noodle is in puppy school. I want to go to puppy school. I mean, I want a puppy for puppy school.
entries.highlight: Met Mateo's new puppy Noodle and tried to teach her tricks.

entries.title: Smash rematch with Jack
entries.body: Jack came over and we played Smash Brothers in the morning. Jack is the best at Fox. We played best of five and he won three to two. Last winter I would have unplugged the Switch probably. Today I just said good game and rematch. Then I won the rematch with Link and Jack said rematch. We did that like nine times. I think it ended even. We stopped because we were hungry.
entries.highlight: Played Smash Brothers with Jack, lost a series without getting angry, and kept trading wins.

entries.title: Lake day ride home
entries.body: In the afternoon Jack's mom drove us to the lake for one last summer trip. On the way home everybody was singing really loud and we were all sunburned. Mateo fell asleep with his mouth open and Jack put a Cheeto on his face. Owen sat in the front so he would not get sick. Nobody puked. I went off the big rope swing into the lake. I screamed like Tessa.
entries.highlight: Took a last summer trip to the lake with friends and tried the big rope swing.

entries.title: Getting my desk ready
entries.body: I had to clean my room before school starts. Under the bed I found my swim goggles from camp and my report card from June. Mom said let's make a homework spot. We cleaned off my desk and put a cup for pencils and a little lamp. Mom said a real desk is for real fourth graders. I put my Monster jump picture on the wall above it so I can look at it when homework is hard.
entries.highlight: Cleaned his room and set up a homework desk for fourth grade with his jump photo above it.

entries.title: Same class or not
entries.body: The class lists came out today and Jack is in my class! We are both in Ms. Ruiz's class. Mateo and Owen are in the other fourth grade. So me and Jack went to the park courts and played around the world to celebrate, and Jack won. I said good game, giraffe. He said thank you, shorty. That is our thing now. Honestly I am kind of nervous for fourth grade though.
entries.favorite: Finding out Jack is in my class
entries.highlight: Celebrated learning that Jack is in his fourth-grade class, while still feeling nervous.

entries.title: Last Minecraft Sunday of summer
entries.body: I played Minecraft for like six hours straight. Not really, it was the last Sunday of summer so Mom let me play for two hours. I built a pump track in Minecraft out of dirt blocks and I rode a minecart over it. It is not the same but it was cool. I made a sign that says ANDY'S MONSTER. Tomorrow is the last day of summer and I am so sad about it.
entries.highlight: Built a Minecraft version of the pump track on the last Sunday of summer.

entries.title: Last summer fishing trip
entries.body: Me and Dad went fishing on the last day of summer. We had peanut butter sandwiches and sunflower seeds. I caught a little bass and Dad caught two sunfish. No Big Gary. Dad asked if I was nervous about fourth grade. I said a little bit because people say fourth grade is a lot harder. Dad said you landed the Monster, you can handle long division. I hope so. Then we packed up the buckets and Dad let me carry the tackle box to the car, which is a big job.
entries.favorite: Dad saying I can handle it
entries.highlight: Went fishing with Dad on the last day of summer and talked about nerves about fourth grade.

entries.title: First day of fourth grade
entries.body: First day of school. I am in fourth grade now. Jack is in my class, and we sit at the same table group. Our teacher is Ms. Ruiz and she seems strict. She said no talking during math and she has a timer on the board. But she also has a class turtle named Speedy. She asked us to write about our summer and I wrote about the Monster jump. I wrote a whole page.
entries.highlight: Started fourth grade with Ms. Ruiz, who seems strict, and sat at a table with Jack.

entries.title: First day pancakes tradition
entries.body: Dad made chocolate pancakes for the first day of school. He says it is a tradition now. I ate four even though I was nervous. Tessa ate one and a half because it was her first day of kindergarten too. She was wearing her purple backpack and she did not throw a fit at all. I told her the kindergarten room is the one with the fish tank. She held my hand to the door.
entries.highlight: Had first-day chocolate pancakes and walked Tessa to her kindergarten door.

entries.title: Labor Day weekend at Game Haven
entries.body: Dad took me to Game Haven on Sunday. There is a new expansion out and everybody was opening packs. I got two holos and a lot of junk. I battled a kid named Ruben again, the one who beat me last year. I beat him this time! My deck is way better now because I learned about having enough energy cards. Ruben said nice deck. I showed him my Gardevoir too. We might trade next week.
entries.highlight: Beat a kid at the card shop who had beaten him a year earlier, thanks to an improved deck.

entries.title: Mateo and the Cedar Street hill
entries.body: Me and Mateo went riding after school. My legs are stronger from the pump track so I rode up the Cedar Street hill without walking! Even without gears! Mateo had to click to the easy gear. I said who needs gears. Then I almost fell going down because I went too fast. Not gonna lie, I was scared. We went to Mateo's after and played with Noodle, who tried to eat my bike glove.
entries.highlight: Rode up a big hill without walking for the first time, thanks to stronger legs from the pump track.

entries.title: Dad's new dragon deck
entries.body: Dad and me played Magic the Gathering after homework. Ever since I beat him he made a new deck. It is red and black with even more dragons. He beat me twice. I said that deck is not fair and he said neither was the bear. Ha. I am going to change my deck to have more cards that stop flying creatures. Dad gave me three new cards from his box to help. That is kind of like helping the enemy.
entries.highlight: Lost twice to Dad's new Magic deck and planned changes to his own.

entries.title: The bowl at the skate park
entries.body: I went to the skate park on my scooter on Saturday. I dropped in on the medium ramp and it was easy now. So I tried the bowl. The bowl is like a big empty pool. I rode around the bottom and then up the side and I fell and slid down on my elbows. Ouch. My elbow has a scrape like my knee did in April. I am gonna try again next weekend.
entries.highlight: Tried the skate park bowl for the first time and scraped his elbow.

entries.title: Racing Eli home
entries.body: Me and Eli had a bike race after school, from the school to the stop sign by Eli's house. Eli won by like one bike length. I said good race even though I really thought I would win. Then Biscuit ran out and chased us down the sidewalk. She is so big now, not a puppy anymore. Eli's mom gave us lemonade. Homework was already done, so I did not have to rush home. That is the best feeling.
entries.highlight: Raced Eli home on bikes and said good race after losing by a bike length.

entries.title: Homework done before anyone asked
entries.body: Ms. Ruiz gives way more homework than Mr. Dawson. A multiplication page, a spelling thing, and a science worksheet about rocks. But here is the crazy part. I did half of it in carpool and the rest at my new desk the second I got home, and Mom did not even say anything. She came in and said, did you already start? I said I already finished. She looked at me like I was an alien. Then I played Smash for my whole time and nobody had to argue. Honestly, it was kind of nice.
entries.highlight: Finished all his homework right after school without being reminded, and Mom was surprised.

entries.title: Anti-dragon deck works
entries.body: Dad and me played Magic the Gathering on Sunday afternoon. I changed my green deck like I planned. I put in four spiders that have reach, which means they can block flying creatures. Dad played his big black dragon and I blocked it with a spider and they both died! Dad said, well played. We played three games and I won two. Dad says I am thinking like a real player now because I planned for what he would do. I think I like Magic better than Pokemon now. Maybe. Do not tell Jack.
entries.favorite: Blocking the dragon with a spider
entries.highlight: Rebuilt his Magic deck to counter Dad's dragons and won two of three games.

entries.title: A B on the times tables quiz
entries.body: We had a timed math quiz today on the six, seven and eight times tables. Ms. Ruiz puts the timer on the board and it ticks really loud. I got an 84, which is a B. I was kind of mad because I knew all of them, I just ran out of time on seven times eight. It is fifty six. I know that now forever. Mom made flashcards and we practiced in the car. Also Tessa turns six on Saturday and she wants a mermaid cake. Of course she does.
entries.highlight: Got a B on a timed multiplication quiz and practiced with flashcards to do better.

entries.title: Jafie's trampoline dodgeball
entries.body: I went to Jafie's house on Saturday. His dad finally fixed the hole in the trampoline net. We played trampoline dodgeball with those soft balls and Jafie's little cousins. The cousins were really little so me and Jafie made it fair by only throwing underhand at them. Then we went inside and Jafie showed me his new Pokemon game and his team is so strong now. He has a shiny Garchomp. I said that is sick. We ate popcorn and watched him play the gym leader. He beat it on the first try.
entries.highlight: Played trampoline dodgeball at Jafie's and made the game fair for his little cousins.

entries.title: Helping a little kid at Game Haven
entries.body: Dad took me to Game Haven on Saturday. There was a little kid there who was like seven and he had a deck with almost no energy cards, just like Jafie had in third grade. He kept losing and his face was getting red. So I showed him how to put in more energy and I gave him five of my extras. He won his next game! His dad said thank you to me. Dale at the counter said I am becoming a regular. I felt kind of grown up. Then I lost to Ruben, but it was a close one.
entries.highlight: Helped a younger kid fix his Pokemon deck at the card shop and gave him extra cards.

entries.title: Tessa's shoe meltdown
entries.body: Okay, so this morning was chaos. Tessa threw a fit before school because her shoes felt weird. She said the socks were too bumpy. She took them off like five times and cried and we almost missed carpool. Jack's mom was honking. I told Tessa to wear her rain boots and she stopped crying right away and wore them. It was not even raining. Mom said thank you for the idea. Kindergarten is making her more tired, I think. That is what Mom says too.
entries.highlight: Helped end Tessa's shoe meltdown before school by suggesting she wear rain boots.

entries.title: I rode the whole bowl
entries.body: After school I went to the skate park on my scooter. My elbow is all healed from last month. I tried the bowl again and this time I went all the way around the bottom and up both sides without falling! I did it like six times. The trick is you bend your knees a lot. Then I slipped on my last try and banged my knee a little, but not enough to bleed. A teenager said that was clean. I do not know what clean means but I think it is good.
entries.highlight: Rode the whole skate park bowl several times after falling there a month earlier.

entries.title: Teaching Jack to play Magic
entries.body: Dad and me taught Jack how to play Magic the Gathering. Jack came over after homework and Dad let him borrow the blue deck. Jack was so confused at first because he kept calling it Pokemon. He called mana energy like four times. I explained tapping and flying and blocking. It was weird being the one who knows stuff. Jack beat me once because he got lucky with a big sea monster. I said good game and he said this is actually fun. Now I have someone besides Dad to play with.
entries.highlight: Helped Dad teach Jack to play Magic the Gathering and found a new friend to play with.

entries.title: Dodgeball catch in gym
entries.body: In gym we played dodgeball today. Coach Bell made the teams and I was on the blue side. A big kid named Dale Junior, no relation to card shop Dale, threw a super hard one at me and I caught it! When you catch it the thrower is out and somebody on your team gets to come back in. Jack came back in and gave me a high five. Then I got hit in the leg like ten seconds later. But the catch was the best part. Everybody saw it.
entries.highlight: Caught a hard dodgeball throw in gym, getting a strong player out.

entries.title: Thunder win, finally
entries.body: I had a soccer game after school. It is the fall Thunder team again with yellow shirts. I scored a goal! It was off a corner kick that bounced off my knee, so it was kind of an accident, but it counts. And we won! Three to one! The Thunder never wins. Coach Mike bought us all freeze pops. Last spring we lost every game except one tie. Honestly, I think it is because we practice passing now instead of everybody chasing the ball like bees.
entries.highlight: Scored a goal as his soccer team finally won a game, three to one.

entries.title: Online racing with Jafie
entries.body: After the soccer game Jafie and me played a racing game online from our own houses. We talk on the headset and it is like he is in my room. He kept beating me on the desert track because he knows a shortcut through a cactus field. I made him teach it to me. He said only if you do not use it against me. I used it against him on the next race and he laughed so hard. Mom came in and said it is a school night. Okay, okay.
entries.highlight: Raced Jafie online and learned his secret shortcut.

entries.title: Tournament day carpool
entries.body: On Sunday Jack's mom drove a bunch of us to a soccer tournament an hour away, because Mateo and Jack are on the Thunder with me now. Mateo brought a speaker and played the same song like eight times. Owen came to watch and he sat in the front with a bag just in case. He did not need it. We won one game and lost two at the tournament. On the way home everybody was too tired to sing, so we just ate pretzels.
entries.highlight: Carpooled to a soccer tournament an hour away with friends and teammates.

entries.title: Tessa learns Pokemon cards
entries.body: There was no school today. Tessa asked me to teach her Pokemon cards for real, not just making the cards talk. So I made her a deck with my extras, all fire types because she likes red. I taught her how energy works and how attacking works. She is six now so she can read some of the words. She won one game! I might have let her a little bit. Okay, a lot. But she got really excited and hugged me. Then she asked if she could come to Game Haven. Maybe.
entries.highlight: Taught Tessa to play Pokemon cards with a deck he built for her.

entries.title: Owen jumped the Monster
entries.body: In the afternoon me and Owen went to the pump track. Owen has been practicing all fall and today he tried the Monster! I told him what Eli told me, pump the last two bumps and look where you want to land. He landed it but then he wobbled and fell in the dirt. He got right back up and did it again and landed it perfect. I yelled so loud. I fell once too on the berm turn but I got back up. Owen said thanks for teaching me. That was the best part.
entries.highlight: Coached Owen through his first big pump track jump, the same advice Eli once gave him.

entries.title: One hour of Pokemon, not six
entries.body: I played Pokemon tonight for exactly one hour. Homework first, then I got an hour, then dinner. It is kind of my own rule now too. If I do homework first I do not have to think about it while I play. I am trying to finish the new Pokemon game before Jafie. I have six badges and he has seven. Tonight I caught a Dragonite and named it Big Gary as a joke for Dad. Dad laughed so hard.
entries.highlight: Played an hour of Pokemon after finishing homework, a rule he now follows on his own.

entries.title: Jafie's sneaky steals
entries.body: Me and Jafie played basketball at the park after school. The leaves are falling all over the court so the ball kept bouncing weird. Jafie is still so fast at stealing. He took the ball from me like five times. So I started dribbling with my other hand, like Eli showed me, and he could not get it. I won eleven to eight. We said good game and did our handshake. We have a new handshake with a slap and a snap. I messed up the snap. I always mess up the snap.
entries.highlight: Played basketball with Jafie and used his weaker hand to stop Jafie's steals.

entries.title: Raking leaves for a game fund
entries.body: I had to do chores today. Not my room this time, the leaves. Our backyard was covered. Dad said if I rake the whole yard I get ten dollars. Ten dollars! I raked for like two hours. Okay, forty five minutes. Tessa kept jumping in the piles and wrecking them, but then I started making piles for her on purpose and a separate pile for the bag. I am saving my money for the new Smash character pack. I have twenty three dollars now. I need seven more.
entries.favorite: Making piles for Tessa on purpose
entries.highlight: Raked the backyard to earn money toward a video game and made extra leaf piles for Tessa.

entries.title: Pumpkin carving with Tessa
entries.body: My sister was annoying at first because she did not want to touch the pumpkin guts. She said they look like goopy boogers, which is true. So I scooped hers out for her. Then she drew a face with a marker and I helped her carve it. Hers has three eyes and one tooth. Mine is a creeper face from Minecraft because that is my costume this year. Dad roasted the seeds. Tessa said our pumpkins are best friends. That is kind of a weird thing to say but okay.
entries.highlight: Carved pumpkins with Tessa and helped her with the messy parts.

entries.title: Costume planning at Owen's
entries.body: I went to Owen's house after school to finish our costumes. I am a creeper from Minecraft and Owen is a zombie from Minecraft. We made my creeper head out of a big box and green paper squares. Owen's dog Pickles kept sitting on the paper. Owen's mom said we used a whole bottle of glue. My head is huge and I can only see out of the mouth hole. I bumped into the doorway three times. It is perfect. Halloween is in two days.
entries.highlight: Made a creeper costume out of a box at Owen's house before Halloween.

entries.title: Halloween with the guys
entries.body: Me, Jack and Jafie went trick-or-treating together without parents walking right next to us! Our dads walked way behind on the sidewalk. I was a creeper, Jack was a werewolf, and Jafie was a ninja. My box head got a little smushed by the end. We did the whole neighborhood plus the cul-de-sac with the full-size candy bars. After, we dumped everything on Jack's floor and traded candy. I traded all my candy corn for Jack's peanut butter cups. Best trade of my life. Mateo would say wait a day, but Halloween trades do not count.
entries.highlight: Trick-or-treated with Jack and Jafie with dads walking behind for the first time, then traded candy.

entries.title: Candy fueled card day
entries.body: Dad took me to Game Haven on Saturday and I brought a bag of Halloween candy to share. Dale said I am the best customer ever. I bought the new Smash pack with my leaf money at home first, so I am broke now. At Game Haven I battled Ruben and won, then lost to a high school kid who has a deck that probably costs a hundred dollars. I said good game. He said your deck is solid for a kid. I will take it. Tessa came too and just ate my candy.
entries.highlight: Shared Halloween candy at the card shop and earned praise for his deck from an older player.

entries.title: My idea for screen-free Sunday
entries.body: Mom said no video games today because it is screen free Sunday, like always. But this time I got to pick what we do. I picked a hike at the state park with the big waterfall. Tessa complained the whole first part and then she found a stick that looks like a wand and she was fine. The waterfall was so loud. Dad said I picked well. Honestly, I did not miss the Switch that much. I mean, a little. I thought about Smash on the way home.
entries.highlight: Chose a family hike for screen-free Sunday and found he did not miss games much.

entries.title: Owen's cold court comeback
entries.body: Cold basketball with Owen after school. It is getting cold, so we wore gloves, which makes dribbling impossible. Owen still does his granny shot and it still goes in. He was beating me nine to two. Then I started using my spin move and I came back and won eleven to ten. Owen said good game and that I am annoying. I said thank you. He is less quiet now than he was in third grade. He talks so much at lunch now.
entries.highlight: Came back from far behind to win a cold basketball game against Owen.

entries.title: The great carpool song vote
entries.body: Carpool almost had a war today. A song war. Mateo wanted his song and Jack wanted a different one. So I said let's vote and do the winner first and then the other one. Everybody agreed. Jack's mom said I should be a judge someday. The vote was three to two for Mateo's song. Jack groaned but he sang anyway. Owen sang so loud he coughed. It was a good one.
entries.favorite: Jack's mom saying I should be a judge
entries.highlight: Settled a carpool song argument by suggesting a vote, and everyone agreed.

entries.title: Tessa on my Mario Kart team
entries.body: I played Mario Kart this morning, but the new part is Tessa played with me. I turned on the steering helper so she does not fall off the road. We did team mode, me and her against the computers. She was Peach and I was Bowser. She came in eighth like every time but our team still won the Mushroom Cup because I came in first. She screamed we won and did a dance. I never let her play with me before because she was too slow. It was not that bad.
entries.highlight: Let Tessa play on his Mario Kart team for the first time and won a cup together.

entries.title: Racing Jack after soccer ends
entries.body: Jack came over and we played a racing game. Soccer season is over so we have more time after school. We did a best of ten. Jack is good at the snow tracks and I am good at the desert tracks because of Jafie's cactus shortcut. It ended five to five. We decided ties are okay. Last year a tie would have made me so mad because I wanted to win so bad. Now I think a tie with Jack is honestly kind of perfect. Then we ate cereal for a snack.
entries.highlight: Ended a ten-race series with Jack in a tie and decided he was fine with it.

entries.title: Clean room for the Thanksgiving cousins
entries.body: I had to clean my room because the cousins are staying with us for Thanksgiving and my cousin Danny is sleeping on my floor. Behind my dresser I found a Pokemon card I traded away in third grade. Wait, how? That is a mystery. I put my Magic cards on the high shelf so little Benny cannot lick them. I made Danny a little space with a sleeping bag and my extra pillow. Mom said I am being a good host. That is a word for a person who hosts.
entries.highlight: Cleaned and prepared his room for his cousin's Thanksgiving visit.

entries.title: Jack turns ten at the bowling alley
entries.body: I went to Jack's birthday party at the bowling alley. He is ten now. I am still nine for two months. That is not fair. No bumpers this time, Jack said we are too old.
