I got two strikes and a lot of sevens. Jack got the high score and I said good game, giraffe. We ate pizza and the cake had a bowling pin on it. I gave Jack a Magic deck box with a dragon on it because now he plays too. He said it was the best present.
entries.highlight: Celebrated Jack's tenth birthday at the bowling alley and gave him a Magic deck box.

entries.title: Last one on in dodgeball
entries.body: In gym we played dodgeball and I was the last one on my team! It was me against four kids on the other side. Everybody on my team was yelling my name. I dodged like six balls. I jumped over one. Then I caught one and got Jack back in, and then Jack got hit right away. So it was me again. Then I got hit in the shoulder and we lost. But Coach Bell said that was the best dodging he has seen all year. My heart was beating so fast.
entries.highlight: Was the last player standing in a gym dodgeball game and dodged several throws.

entries.title: Fishing before the turkey
entries.body: No school today because tomorrow is Thanksgiving. Dad took me and Danny fishing at the lake. It was cold and windy. We had turkey sandwiches, which is funny because tomorrow is all turkey. Danny caught nothing. I caught a perch and I put it in the bucket and Danny said cool. Danny is thirteen now so when he says cool it is a big deal. Dad told Danny about Big Gary and Danny believed it right away. I said I saw him jump in July. That is true.
entries.highlight: Fished with Dad and his cousin before Thanksgiving and caught a perch.

entries.title: Thanksgiving kids table
entries.body: Today was Thanksgiving. Tessa was a lot at first, because she wanted to sit next to me and so did Benny, and she threw a fit. So I sat between them. That was a mistake, they both wanted my rolls. But then after dinner me and Tessa and Danny and Benny built a hideout in the basement out of the folding chairs and the guest blankets. Tessa was the captain again. Everybody had to say what they are thankful for. I said my friends, my bike, and Big Gary.
entries.highlight: Sat between Tessa and a cousin at Thanksgiving and built a hideout with the kids afterward.

entries.title: Magic with Dad and Jack
entries.body: Dad, Jack and me played Magic the Gathering, three players at once, which is called free for all. It is so chaotic. Jack attacked me and I attacked Dad and Dad attacked both of us with his dragon. Then me and Jack made a deal to both attack Dad. Dad said that is not fair. We said it is strategy. We beat him! Then Jack beat me at the end. I said good game and Jack said you made it close. Dad said he is never doing three players again.
entries.highlight: Played a chaotic three-player Magic game with Dad and Jack and teamed up to beat Dad.

entries.title: Eli's Pokemon game rematch
entries.body: Eli came over and we played Pokemon battles on the Switch. Me and Eli made full teams. I won the first two because my Dragonite, the one named Big Gary, is really strong now. Then Eli beat me with a weird bug type I never even heard of. I said that bug is crazy, good game. We traded some Pokemon too. I gave him a shiny Magikarp because he collects them. He gave me a fire one. We both said it was a fair trade. The napkin rule lives on.
entries.highlight: Battled and traded Pokemon fairly with Eli on the Switch.

entries.title: Noodle can sit now
entries.body: I went to Mateo's house on Sunday. Noodle graduated from puppy school! She can sit and shake now. Mateo showed me and she did it for a cracker. Then she ran off with Mateo's sock. We built a ramp out of cardboard in his driveway for our bikes, but it was too cold and slippery, so we went inside. We played Minecraft on his computer and built a giant statue of Noodle. Her ears are made out of brown wool. I still want a dog. Mom still says no.
entries.highlight: Saw Mateo's dog do tricks and built a Minecraft statue of her.

entries.title: The great Lego cleanout
entries.body: Room cleaning day again. Mom said I have too many Legos for one floor. So we sorted them. I kept the good sets and put the random pieces in a big box. Then I decided to give some of my old little-kid Legos to Tessa, like the big blocks and the farm set. She was so happy she screamed. Then she said thank you Andy in a weird robot voice. I found three missing socks under the bed. Again. My bed eats socks. Science cannot explain it.
entries.highlight: Sorted his Legos while cleaning and gave his old sets to Tessa.

entries.title: First shoveling job
entries.body: It snowed last night, like four inches! But it was not a snow day, so that is unfair. After school my chore was shoveling the driveway with Dad. It was so heavy. Dad said if I shovel the old lady next door's driveway too, she might pay me. I did and she gave me five dollars and a cookie. A whole cookie. I am saving for the new Pokemon expansion box. Shoveling is the worst but money is the best. My arms are so tired I can barely talk.
entries.highlight: Shoveled snow with Dad and earned five dollars from the neighbor.

entries.title: Snow wall at Owen's
entries.body: I went to Owen's house after school and there was still snow, so we made a snow wall in his front yard. Owen's brother helped us make the walls tall. Pickles kept jumping in the snow and disappearing, which was so funny. Then we had a snowball fight with the kids across the street. We won because our wall was stronger. Owen made the best snowballs because he packs them really hard. My gloves got soaked. His mom made hot chocolate with the tiny marshmallows.
entries.highlight: Built a snow wall and won a snowball fight at Owen's house.

entries.title: Lunch table Magic league
entries.body: At lunch we battled with our cards, but now some of us play Magic instead of Pokemon. Me, Jack, and now Mateo has a deck too. Ms. Ruiz said we can play at the end of lunch if we clean up. We made a little league and I wrote down the scores on a piece of notebook paper. I am winning, eight wins and three losses. Jafie still plays Pokemon and says Magic is for dads. That is kind of true. My dad plays it. Ha.
entries.highlight: Started a lunchtime Magic league with friends and kept track of the scores himself.

entries.title: Dodgeball against the other class
entries.body: In gym we played dodgeball against the other fourth grade class, which has Mateo and Owen. It was so intense. I was the last one on my team again! But this time it was against Owen. We were throwing back and forth and then I caught his ball. We won! Owen said good game and then said I am annoying, again. Coach Bell said he wants to see more teamwork though, not just me dodging. Fair. Next time I will pass the ball to Jack more.
entries.highlight: Won a dodgeball game against the other class by catching Owen's throw as the last one standing.

entries.title: Christmas card picture meltdown
entries.body: Christmas card picture day, which is honestly the worst day of the year. We had to take our Christmas card picture in matching sweaters, and Tessa threw a fit because her sweater was itchy. She cried for like twenty minutes. Every picture she had a mad face. So I started making the creeper sound and doing silly faces behind the camera, and finally she laughed. The picture where she is laughing is the one Mom picked. My eyes are closed in it though. Mom said that is the price of being a good brother.
entries.highlight: Made Tessa laugh during a frustrating Christmas card photo shoot.

entries.title: Christmas and the bike with gears
entries.body: Christmas! I woke up at six thirty, which Mom said is better than last year. I got a new bike with gears! It is black and green and it has eighteen speeds. I asked for gears back in May after I tried Mateo's, and Santa remembered, or Mom and Dad remembered. I also got the new Pokemon expansion box. My flame helmet does not fit anymore, so Dad got me a new one that is matte black. Tessa got a bigger speaker for her karaoke machine. Oh no. Again. I gave Tessa a mermaid stuffy that I bought with my shoveling money. She named it Andy Junior.
entries.highlight: Got a geared bike and a new helmet for Christmas and gave Tessa a gift bought with his own money.

entries.title: Christmas afternoon at the pond
entries.body: After presents and lunch, Dad took me fishing at the lake for like an hour, just us. That is our Christmas thing now I guess. I gave Dad a new lure that looks like a little frog. I picked it out at the store with Mom. He said it is the best lure he ever got. It was so cold the edges of the lake had ice, so we fished from the end of the dock. We caught nothing. Dad said Big Gary is on Christmas vacation too. We drank hot chocolate from the thermos like last winter.
entries.highlight: Went on a short Christmas fishing trip with Dad and gave him a lure he picked out.

entries.title: Sledding instead of screens
entries.body: Mom said no video games today because I played the new Pokemon expansion stuff all night yesterday. I was going to complain but then it snowed again. So me and Tessa went sledding at the big hill by the school. I pulled her up the hill on the sled like ten times because her legs are short. Then we did a double run together and crashed into a snowbank. Tessa had snow in her hood and she was laughing so hard. Okay, no screens was not that bad. Do not tell Mom I said that.
entries.highlight: Went sledding with Tessa on a no-screens day and pulled her up the hill.

entries.title: Minecraft Christmas village
entries.body: I played Minecraft for like six hours straight. Not really, it is winter break so it was probably three hours with breaks. I built a whole Christmas village with Jafie on the server. There is a candy cane house, a giant tree with lights made of glowstone, and an ice skating rink. Jafie built a snowman that is like fifty blocks tall. Then a creeper blew up the candy cane house. Last year I would have screamed. This year I just laughed and rebuilt it with stone this time. Smarter.
entries.highlight: Built a Minecraft Christmas village with Jafie and calmly rebuilt after a creeper blew part of it up.

entries.title: Owen's brother's old Magic cards
entries.body: I went to Owen's house during winter break. Owen got a new video game but we did not even play it much. His brother found a box of old Magic cards in the basement and said we could have some! There was a really old card with a picture of a giant wurm that Dad will go crazy about. We split the cards fair, one for you, one for me, like a draft. Then we went down to the Lego city and it is even bigger now. There is a stadium.
entries.highlight: Split a box of old Magic cards fairly with Owen during winter break.

entries.title: New Year's Eve free throws
entries.body: Me and Jafie played basketball at the rec center because it was too cold outside. They had a New Year's Eve open gym for kids. We did a free throw contest, and I made eleven in a row, which crushes my old record from last year when I made six at the park. Jafie made nine. Then we played a pick up game with some older kids and they let us play. At night I stayed up until midnight for the first time and banged a pot with a spoon. Tessa fell asleep at nine.
entries.highlight: Beat his free throw record at a New Year's Eve open gym and stayed up until midnight for the first time.

entries.title: My own homework plan
entries.body: It is still winter break but I made a New Year's thing today. I made my own homework plan on my whiteboard. Mom did not even ask me to. It says: Monday to Thursday, homework right after snack, then reading twenty minutes, then games. Friday is free. I drew a little Monster jump at the bottom for luck. Last year I fought Mom about homework first like every day. Now I kind of get it. If I do it first, my brain is free. Mom took a picture of the whiteboard and sent it to Grandma. That is a little embarrassing.
entries.favorite: Drawing the Monster jump on it
entries.highlight: Made his own homework schedule on a whiteboard without being asked, a change from last year's arguments.

entries.title: Two on two at the rec center
entries.body: Me and Eli played basketball at the rec center on Sunday. We played two on two against Eli's cousin and his friend, who are in sixth grade. They are so tall. We lost the first game by a lot. Then we figured out that if I drive and pass to Eli in the corner, he is open every time. We lost the second game too but only by two. Eli said that was a good plan. I said I learned it from Coach Bell talking about teamwork. The sixth graders said good game, little guys.
entries.highlight: Played two-on-two against older kids with Eli and came up with a passing plan that nearly worked.

entries.title: The lunch league standings
entries.body: At lunch we battled with our cards. The Magic lunch league has five people now because Owen joined with his brother's old cards. I keep the standings on notebook paper in my binder. Jack is in first place now, nine and three, and I am in second. I was kind of mad when I wrote it down, but I wrote it down right. Mateo said I should cheat on the standings and I said no way, that is not how a league works. Ms. Ruiz said she likes how organized I am.
entries.highlight: Kept honest standings for the lunchtime Magic league, even when he fell to second place.

entries.title: Birthday planning on a no screen night
entries.body: Mom said no video games tonight because I stayed up late on the Switch last weekend. So I used the time to plan my birthday sleepover. I will be ten! Double digits! I made a bracket on paper for the Smash tournament. Everybody plays everybody once in the first round, then the top four go to semifinals. I made rules too. No picking the same stage every time, and everybody says good game after each match. Dad said it looks like a real tournament. I made Tessa the official announcer.
entries.highlight: Spent a no-screens night planning a fair Smash bracket and rules for his tenth birthday.

entries.title: Magic prerelease with Dad
entries.body: Dad took me to a Magic prerelease at Game Haven, which is when you get to play with new cards before they come out in stores. You open packs and build a deck right there. I was the youngest one there! Everybody else was teenagers or grown ups. I won two games and lost two. One guy with a beard said I am a better player than his brother. Dad was so proud he kept telling people I am his son. That was a little embarrassing too. But mostly it was so cool.
entries.highlight: Played in a Magic prerelease with Dad as the youngest player and went two and two.

entries.title: My tenth birthday sleepover
entries.body: My birthday sleepover! I am ten now. Jack, Jafie, Mateo, Owen and Eli all came again, five friends like last year. We had two pizzas. I asked for three this time, which is more realistic than a hundred, but Mom said two plus wings. Then we did my Smash tournament with my bracket. Tessa announced every match in a sports voice. I lost in the semifinals to Eli and I said good game and I meant it. Last year I hid in the bathroom when I lost. Jack won the whole thing. The cake had a Monster jump on it.
entries.highlight: Turned ten with a five-friend sleepover and ran his own Smash bracket, losing in the semifinals graciously.

entries.title: One a.m. rematch with Eli
entries.body: After everybody fell asleep, me and Eli were still awake. It was like one in the morning. We turned the TV volume down to two and did a secret Smash rematch. He picked Kirby like always and I picked Link like always. I won! Then he won. Then we heard Mom on the stairs and we pretended to be asleep with the controllers still in our hands. She knew. She just said happy birthday, now sleep. We laughed into our pillows so hard. That was my favorite part of the whole birthday, honestly.
entries.highlight: Played a secret late-night Smash rematch with Eli after his birthday sleepover.

entries.title: Birthday Minecraft and no school
entries.body: No school today because of Martin Luther King Day, which is perfect after a sleepover. I played Minecraft for like six hours straight. Not really, I fell asleep on the couch for one of the hours. I used my birthday money for a Minecraft texture pack that makes everything look realistic. The water looks so real. I built a lake and put a giant fish in it made of blocks and named it Big Gary. Dad said that is the closest he will ever get to seeing him.
entries.highlight: Relaxed on the school holiday after his birthday and built a Minecraft lake with a block version of Big Gary.

entries.title: Sleepover cleanup duty
entries.body: I had to clean up after the sleepover. Mom said a ten year old can clean up his own party. There were pizza crusts under the couch and popcorn in the sleeping bags. Somebody, probably Owen, spilled soda on the rug. I found two socks that were not even mine, so now other people's socks disappear at my house too. I also found a note from Tessa that said best birthday brother. I put it in my Pokemon binder. It took an hour. Mom said thank you for doing it without complaining. I complained a little in my head.
entries.highlight: Cleaned up after his birthday sleepover without complaining and found a sweet note from Tessa.

entries.title: Carpool birthday song, late
entries.body: Carpool today was a concert, and the song was happy birthday to me even though my birthday was four days ago. Jack started it and everybody joined in. They did the cha cha cha part. Then Mateo said I still owe him a rematch from the tournament. I said anytime. Jack's mom told us her car is retiring soon and she is getting a new one. Everybody was sad. That minivan has so many memories. Like Owen puking. Nobody puked today though.
entries.highlight: His carpool friends sang him a late happy birthday, and they learned the old minivan is being replaced.

entries.title: Power outage game night
entries.body: We did not have any video games today, but not because of Mom. A big ice storm knocked out the power! The whole house was dark at dinner. Dad lit candles and we played Uno on the kitchen table with flashlights. Tessa kept saying Uno when she had like five cards. Dad said that is a strategy. It is not. Then we played the trading sheep game and I won again. Not gonna lie, it was kind of cozy. The power came back at nine and the house beeped everywhere and it made us all jump.
entries.highlight: Played board games by candlelight with his family during an ice storm power outage.

entries.title: Iced up dock fishing
entries.body: The ice storm was yesterday, but Dad still wanted to fish, so we went to the lake. Everything was covered in ice and the trees looked like glass. We only fished for like thirty minutes from the dock because it was freezing. We had our salami sandwiches though. I tried the frog lure I gave Dad for Christmas and something nibbled it! We did not catch it but it counts as a sign. Dad said the frog lure is lucky. I said it is not lucky if we never catch anything. He said patience. Patience is so hard.
entries.highlight: Fished briefly with Dad on an icy morning and felt a nibble on the Christmas lure.

entries.title: Tessa's first Game Haven trip
entries.body: In the afternoon Dad took me and Tessa to Game Haven. It was Tessa's first time. She brought her fire deck that I made her. I helped her play a game against another little kid. She won! Dale gave her a promo card because it was her first time. She held it with two hands like it was made of gold. Then I played Ruben and lost a close one. I said good game. Tessa said good game too even though she was not playing. She copies me now. It is kind of funny.
entries.favorite: Tessa winning her first game there
entries.highlight: Took Tessa to the card shop for the first time and coached her to a win.

entries.title: Owen's surprise wurm play
entries.body: At lunch we battled with our cards. Owen played that old giant wurm card from his brother's box and it beat me! I had no way to block something that big. Everybody at the table went crazy because Owen never wins. He just started. I said good game, that card is honestly insane. Owen was smiling so big. I wrote his win in the standings with a star next to it because it was his first one. Jack said stars are not official. I said I am the commissioner, so they are.
entries.highlight: Lost to Owen's rare card at lunch and celebrated Owen's first Magic league win.

entries.title: Snow day sculpture
entries.body: It was a snow day! No school! But Mom said no video games until lunch because it is a snow day, not a screen day. So me and Tessa built a snowman, except we made it look like a creeper, all square. It was so hard to make the snow square. Then Dad helped us make a ramp out of snow and we sledded off it in the backyard. I went really high, like a mini Monster jump. Tessa went over it and screamed so loud the neighbor dog barked. Then I got Switch time after lunch. Perfect day.
entries.highlight: Built a square creeper snowman and a sled ramp with Tessa on a snow day.

entries.title: Noodle's sweater
entries.body: I went to Mateo's house on Sunday. Noodle has a sweater now because wiener dogs get cold. It has stripes and she looks so funny. We played Mateo's new soccer video game and I lost every game. I did not even get mad. Mateo is just better at that one and I am better at Smash. That is fair. Then we made a plan for spring soccer. Coach Mike is still coaching the Thunder. Mateo said we should practice our passing on his driveway when the snow melts.
entries.highlight: Lost a soccer video game to Mateo without getting upset and planned spring soccer practice.

entries.title: Tuesday surprise pancakes
entries.body: Dad made chocolate pancakes on a Tuesday, which never happens. He said it was because he got a promotion at work. I ate four. Tessa stayed totally calm, even though Dad put blueberries in hers, which she usually hates. She said she likes blueberries now because she is six. I said that makes no sense and she said yes it does. Then we had to rush to carpool in the new car. Jack's mom got a new SUV. It smells like plastic. It is weird but fine.
entries.highlight: Had celebration pancakes for Dad's promotion before riding in carpool's new car.

entries.title: Making room for trophies
entries.body: I had to clean my room. I found a Magic card under the bed that was bent in half, which is a tragedy. But the big thing is I moved my desk to the other wall so the shelf can be over my bed. I put my soccer medals and my fourth place Pokemon promo and the picture of the Monster jump on it. Mom said it looks like a real teenager room. I am ten, not a teenager. But okay. It does look really good.
entries.highlight: Rearranged his room and made a shelf to display his medals and keepsakes.

entries.title: Tessa's tooth fit
entries.body: Big news in our house. Tessa has her first loose tooth and she threw a fit every time anybody went near it. She would not eat lunch because it wiggled. She cried at the sandwich. So I told her when I lost my first tooth I was scared too and I bit an apple and it popped out and did not even hurt. That is true. She bit an apple and it did not come out, but she stopped crying. Then later it fell out in her mashed potatoes. She screamed. Then she was so proud.
entries.favorite: The tooth in the mashed potatoes
entries.highlight: Calmed Tessa about her first loose tooth by sharing his own story, and it fell out at dinner.

entries.title: Minecraft roller coaster with Owen
entries.body: Owen came over after school and we played Minecraft. We built a roller coaster that goes through a mountain and over a lava lake. It took forever to get the rails right. Owen is really good at building because of all the Lego. He made a loop, which you cannot really do in Minecraft, but he made it look like one. I made the station with a ticket booth. We rode it like twenty times. Then my timer went off and I turned it off without arguing. Owen said your mom is strict. I said it is my timer.
entries.highlight: Built a Minecraft roller coaster with Owen and stopped when his own timer went off.

entries.title: I was captain and picked Caleb first
entries.body: In gym we played dodgeball and Coach Bell made me a team captain for the first time. There is a kid named Caleb who always gets picked last because he is not that fast. I picked him first. Everybody looked at me weird. Then Caleb got out like right away, but at the end he caught a ball and got me back in, and we won! Caleb was so happy. Coach Bell said captain choice of the year. I was the last one on two times. It was a great gym class, honestly.
entries.highlight: Picked the classmate who is usually chosen last first as dodgeball captain, and Caleb's catch helped them win.

entries.title: Dad's work story by the lake
entries.body: On Friday Dad picked me up after school and we drove straight to the lake. It was not freezing for once, just cold. We sat on our buckets. Dad told me about his new job at work. He is in charge of people now. He said the hardest part is being fair to everybody. I said that is like being commissioner of the lunch league. He laughed and said exactly. I caught a sunfish and Dad caught a big crappie. No Big Gary. We had sandwiches and the orange crackers. I like when Dad tells me grown up stuff.
entries.favorite: Dad telling me grown up stuff
entries.highlight: Fished with Dad and compared Dad's new leadership job to running the lunch league.

entries.title: Presidents Day Mario Kart grand prix
entries.body: No school because of Presidents Day. I did my project first, then I played Mario Kart. Me, Tessa and Dad did a family grand prix. Tessa is way better now. She still uses the steering helper but she came in sixth instead of eighth. Dad came in last because he keeps driving off the rainbow road. I won but I let Tessa have the gold trophy picture because she did the most improving. Dad said that is real sportsmanship.
entries.highlight: Raced a family Mario Kart grand prix on a school holiday after finishing his project, and praised Tessa's improvement.

entries.title: The state report project
entries.body: Even on a day off there is homework, because we have a big state report due Friday, and I got Alaska. Mom says I need to study if I want to go to college, which she says every time. But I already started it last week. Today I did the part about animals. Alaska has moose and bears and salmon. Dad said salmon fishing in Alaska is his dream. I added a fact about that for him. I finished my poster before lunch. Ms. Ruiz said we get extra points for drawing a map. I drew a really good map.
entries.highlight: Worked ahead on his Alaska state report and finished his poster before lunch on a day off.

entries.title: Tessa read me a book
entries.body: My sister was kind of annoying today because she would not stop asking me to listen to her read. She is learning to read in kindergarten. But then I listened and she read a whole book by herself! It was about a frog and a toad. She got stuck on the word because, so I helped her sound it out. Last summer I read her the book about the pig on the moon. Now she reads to me. That is weird. She said next she will read a chapter book. I said do not get crazy.
entries.highlight: Listened to Tessa read a whole book for the first time and helped her sound out words.

entries.title: Pizza night debate
entries.body: We had pizza for dinner on Saturday. I had seconds, and then thirds of the crust part. We had a family debate about pineapple on pizza. Dad and me say no way. Mom and Tessa say yes. Tessa only says yes because Mom says yes. I made everybody give their reasons like a real debate, which Ms. Ruiz taught us. Mom said pineapple is sweet and salty, which is a good reason, but I still think it is wrong. We tied two to two. Then we watched a movie about a racing snail.
entries.highlight: Ran a playful family debate about pineapple on pizza using skills from school.

entries.title: Friday night Smash at Jafie's
entries.body: On Friday I went to Jafie's and we played Smash Brothers for two hours, which for me is a lot on one night. Jafie got really good with a new character, the guy with the swords. He beat me four times in a row and I could tell I was getting frustrated, so I said let's take a break, and we went and jumped on the trampoline in the cold. Then I came back and beat him once. Taking a break works. Mom told me that. Do not tell her it worked.
entries.favorite: Taking a break and coming back
entries.highlight: Noticed his frustration during Smash, took a break on his own, and came back to win a match.

entries.title: Mario Kart after the math test
entries.body: I played Mario Kart for like six hours straight. Okay, really it was one hour, it is a Tuesday. But I earned it. We had a big math test on long division today, which I was really nervous about because long division has so many steps. Divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. Ms. Ruiz taught us to say Does McDonald's Sell Burgers to remember it. I think I did really good. So I played Mario Kart with Tessa as a celebration and we got first place in team mode. She picked Peach like always. Next week I find out my grade.
entries.highlight: Took a long division test he worked hard for and celebrated with an hour of Mario Kart with Tessa.

entries.title: Taco night and the math grade
entries.body: We had tacos for dinner, and I had seconds because I got my math test back. I got a 94 on long division! Ms. Ruiz wrote great improvement on the top with a smiley face. In September I got an 84 on times tables and I was so mad. I asked if we could have tacos to celebrate and Mom said yes. I had three hard shell tacos and one soft one. Dad said I am a math guy now. I am not sure about that. But a 94 is really good. I put the test on the fridge with the pizza magnet.
entries.highlight: Celebrated a 94 on his long division test with taco night, a big jump from earlier in the year.

entries.title: Jack's new Pokemon team
entries.body: Jack came over after school and we played Pokemon on the Switch. Jack has the new game and he built a team with all water types. I said that is risky because grass beats water, and he said that is why he has an ice one too. We did six battles and it was three to three. Then we traded. I gave him a fire one and he gave me a dragon. We did the napkin rule but on my phone notes instead of a napkin. Jack said we are the most fair traders in the whole school. Probably true.
entries.highlight: Battled and traded Pokemon with Jack, still using the old fair-trade rule from third grade.

entries.title: The great closet project
entries.body: I had to clean my room again. It took forever because Mom said this time we do the closet too. I found a whole box of old toys and the creeper box head from Halloween. It is so smushed. Mom said I can only keep one box of little kid stuff. So I made a pile to donate and a pile for Tessa. I gave Tessa my old Pokemon plush and she screamed. I kept the creeper head. Some things are history. Mom said it was the most mature room cleaning ever.
entries.highlight: Cleaned out his closet, donated old toys and passed some to Tessa.

entries.title: Pacer test instead of dodgeball
entries.body: In gym we were supposed to play dodgeball but instead Coach Bell made us do the pacer test. It is the one where you run back and forth until the beeps get too fast. Everybody hates it. I did forty one laps! Last year I think I did twenty something. I think the pump track and soccer made my legs stronger. Jack did forty five and Caleb did thirty, which is his best ever. We cheered for him. Then we got to play dodgeball for the last ten minutes. I got out first. Ha.
entries.highlight: Ran 41 laps on the pacer test, beating last year's score, and cheered on a classmate.

entries.title: Eli's Smash comeback strategy
entries.body: Eli came over and we played Smash Brothers. It is getting so close between us now. Eli beat me with Kirby the first two games, so I watched how he plays. He always jumps right after he gets hit. So I waited for him to jump and then attacked. I won the next three! Eli said how did you figure that out. I said I studied you like a scientist. He said that is creepy. We both laughed. I said good game and he said good game and then we got pizza bagels from the freezer.
entries.highlight: Figured out Eli's Smash pattern and adjusted his strategy to win three games.

entries.title: First gear ride with Mateo
entries.body: After Eli left, Mateo came over with his bike. It is the first warm day, so I finally got to really ride my Christmas bike with gears. We went up the Cedar Street hill and I used the easy gear and it was so easy I could talk the whole time. Mateo said now we are even. Then we rode all the way to the pump track just to look. The Monster is still there. Mud everywhere though. We said we will come back tomorrow when it dries. I cannot wait.
entries.favorite: Talking all the way up the hill
entries.highlight: Rode his new geared bike with Mateo on the first warm day and planned a pump track return.

entries.title: Teaching the little kids to pump
entries.body: We went to the pump track on Saturday and the dirt was finally dry. In the spring it gets super crowded. There were three little kids there, like six or seven, and they kept pedaling on the bumps instead of pumping. One of them fell and started crying. So I went over and showed them how to push the bike down on the front of the bump and pull up on the back. I did it slow so they could see. By the end two of them did the whole small loop without pedaling! Their mom said thank you so much. Not gonna lie, I felt like Eli when he taught me. Then I did the Monster three times to show off a little. Just a little.
entries.highlight: Taught three young kids how to pump at the pump track, the way Eli once taught him.

entries.title: Eli's driveway hoop is back
entries.body: In the afternoon me and Eli played basketball at his house because his dad finally put the hoop back up after winter. Biscuit lay in the grass and watched us like a referee. We played one on one to fifteen. Eli has gotten really good at fadeaways, where you jump backward while you shoot. I tried it and it went over the garage. Twice. Eli was laughing so hard he could not breathe. I won fifteen to thirteen anyway, because I kept driving to the hoop. We said good game and did our handshake, and Eli finally got the snap part right. It took him like a year. I told him I am proud of him in a dad voice. He threw the ball at me.
entries.highlight: Played one-on-one with Eli on his newly restored hoop and won a close game.

entries.title: A screen-free St. Patrick's Day
entries.body: Mom said no video games today. Not as a punishment, just because we had a lot going on, and honestly I did not even argue. I wore my green shirt so nobody could pinch me, and Jack pinched me anyway and said it was not green enough. After homework I read the new book in my BMX graphic novel series. The kid in the book finally lands a backflip and I read that part three times. Then I helped Tessa make a leprechaun trap out of a shoebox and a ladder made of popsicle sticks. She put a gold chocolate coin in it. In the morning I am going to put a tiny footprint in glitter next to it. She will freak out. That is the best part of being a big brother.
entries.highlight: Spent a screen-free evening reading and helping Tessa build a leprechaun trap.

entries.title: Jack's backyard ramp plan
entries.body: I went to Jack's house after school. His dad has a bunch of old wood in the garage, and we asked if we could build a bike ramp. He said yes if we wear helmets and if he helps with the saw. So we drew a plan on graph paper first. I learned that from Ms. Ruiz, measure twice. Jack wanted it super tall and I said we should start small and make it bigger later, like the pump track. We built a little one that is like a foot tall. We each did it ten times. Jack's dog Pepper chased us every single time. Then Jack's mom made grilled cheese with tomato soup. Jack said next week we add a second level. I said only if it passes inspection.
entries.highlight: Built a small bike ramp with Jack and his dad after drawing plans on graph paper.

entries.title: Dad and the first spring bass
entries.body: Saturday morning fishing with Dad. It was the first time it felt like spring there, with birds everywhere and the water all sparkly. We had our sandwiches, and I brought the sunflower seeds this time because I remembered. I caught a largemouth bass that was really big, like longer than my forearm. Dad had to help me with the net. It was my biggest fish ever! We took a picture and let it go. Dad said maybe Big Gary sent his cousin to say hi. We talked about my state report and Dad's Alaska dream. I said when I am older I will go to Alaska with him and catch a salmon. He said that is a deal. We shook on it, with fishy hands.
entries.highlight: Caught his biggest bass ever with Dad and made a plan to fish in Alaska together someday.

entries.title: Spring break pancake bar
entries.body: It is spring break! Dad took the day off work and made chocolate pancakes. But this time he made a pancake bar on the counter with bowls of stuff, like strawberries, whipped cream, chocolate chips and sprinkles. Tessa was so chill, even when she spilled the sprinkles all over the floor. She just said oops and laughed. Last year that would have been a giant meltdown. I made a pancake that looked like the Monster jump with a strawberry bike on top. I ate four, which ties my record. Tessa ate two, which is her new record. Then Dad said we are going to the trampoline park after. Best spring break Monday ever, honestly.
entries.highlight: Built creative pancakes at Dad's spring break pancake bar while Tessa stayed calm after a spill.

entries.title: Wing night with the hot sauce challenge
entries.body: We had chicken wings for dinner. Dad got three kinds, honey barbecue, garlic parmesan, and a hot one called Inferno. I had seconds of the barbecue. Then I did the challenge. Last year I tried one spicy wing and drank a whole glass of milk. This year I ate a whole Inferno wing. My face got so red and my eyes were watering and my nose was running. Dad was timing it. I made it two minutes before drinking milk. Dad said that is a new family record. Tessa ate only plain ones with ranch and said we are both crazy. Mom said this is not a real sport. Dad said it is now.
entries.highlight: Ate a very spicy wing at dinner and lasted two minutes before drinking milk.

entries.title: Long ride to the lake with Mateo
entries.body: On Saturday me and Mateo had a big idea. We asked if we could ride the bike path all the way to the lake. It is like three miles. Mom said yes if we text when we get there. We had to go up Cedar Street hill and then along the creek. My gears helped so much. We saw a heron standing in the water like a statue. When we got to the lake I texted Mom and she sent a thumbs up. We sat on Dad's fishing dock and ate granola bars. Mateo said this is the farthest he has ever biked. Me too. On the way back my legs were burning but it was the good kind of burning.
entries.highlight: Rode three miles with Mateo to the lake, the farthest he had ever biked, with Mom's permission.

entries.title: Back from break carpool
entries.body: Carpool was so loud today because it was the first day back from spring break and everybody was hyper. We sang the song from the movie we all saw, but Jafie only knew half the words, so he made up the rest about pizza. Then everybody told what they did for break. Owen went to the beach and got sunburned. Mateo went to his grandma's. Jack went nowhere but he beat a whole video game. I told them about my bass. They did not believe how big it was so I showed them the picture. Owen said that is basically Big Gary. Jack's mom said she is so glad the new car is still clean.
entries.highlight: Shared spring break stories in carpool and showed friends a photo of his big fish.

entries.title: April Fools pizza
entries.body: We had pizza for dinner, but first I did an April Fools prank. I told everybody I made dinner and put out a plate of cookies cut into triangles with red frosting, like pizza. Tessa believed it was real pizza for like five seconds. Then Dad brought out the real pizza and it was so good. I ate three slices. Then Dad tricked me back. He said I had to do the dishes for a month because of a new rule. I believed him! He said April Fools. Then Mom said actually, he does have to do the dishes tonight. That one was not a joke. I did them. Pranks are fun until you get pranked back.
entries.highlight: Pranked his family with a fake cookie pizza and got pranked back by Dad.

entries.title: Easter party at Grandma's
entries.body: Today was Easter and we had a big party at Grandma's house with all the cousins. Danny is fourteen now and he said he is too old for the egg hunt. So me and Danny hid the eggs for the little kids instead. I hid one in the mailbox and one on top of the swing set. Tessa found nineteen eggs, which is how many I found last Easter. She was so happy. Benny found the mailbox one. Then Danny and me played Magic on Grandma's porch, because Danny started playing too! He beat me one time and I beat him two times. I said good game and he said you are really good for ten. Then we had ham and Grandma's famous rolls. I ate five.
entries.highlight: Helped hide Easter eggs for the younger cousins and played Magic with his teenage cousin.

entries.title: Helping Jack with fractions
entries.body: Fractions are back, but harder. We are doing adding fractions with different denominators, which is so confusing at first. Mom says I need to study if I want to go to college, but this time I was already studying. Then Jack called me on video because he was stuck and almost crying. It was weird because Jack is usually better at school stuff. So I explained it like Mom explained fractions to me in third grade, with pizzas. If one pizza is cut into fourths and one is cut into eighths, you have to cut the fourths more so they match. He got it! He said you should be a teacher. I said maybe. We both finished before dinner. It felt really good to be the one who helps.
entries.highlight: Helped Jack understand fractions over video call, using the pizza method Mom once used with him.

entries.title: Eli's birthday planning
entries.body: I went to Eli's house after school. His birthday is next weekend and he asked me to help plan it, which means I am his main guy. We decided on a Mario Kart tournament, because that is what he wants, and I said I would make the bracket like at my birthday. We made a list of who to invite. Eli wanted to make it a rule that nobody can use the blue shell in the final. I said that is the most fair rule ever. Biscuit kept stealing the paper with the bracket on it, so now it has a bite mark. We kept it anyway. Eli's mom brought us apple slices with peanut butter. Then we practiced on Eli's Switch for the rest of the time.
entries.favorite: Biscuit's bite mark on the bracket
entries.highlight: Helped Eli plan his birthday Mario Kart tournament and offered to make the bracket.

entries.title: The dodgeball catch that won it
entries.body: In gym we played dodgeball and it was boys against girls, which Coach Bell never does. The girls were winning by a lot because Harper throws so hard. I caught a ball and got Jack back in, and then Jack caught one and got Caleb back in. It was like a chain. In the end it was me and Caleb against Harper. Caleb dodged and then I caught Harper's ball and we won! Everybody screamed. Harper said good game and that next time she is aiming at my face. I said fair. Coach Bell said that was the best teamwork all year, which is way better than him saying I dodged a lot, like last year. I think I am a better teammate now.
entries.highlight: Won a close gym dodgeball game through teamwork with Jack and Caleb, earning praise from the coach.

entries.title: Jack has a jump shot now
entries.body: Jack and me hit the park courts after school. Jack has been watching videos and now he has a real jump shot, with his elbow in and everything. It goes in so much. He beat me eleven to seven. I said good game, giraffe, like always. He said thanks, shorty, like always. But then he showed me how to do it and I tried it like thirty times. My elbow kept going out. By the end I made like four in a row. We talked about fifth grade. They say fifth grade is when you start being the oldest in the school. Jack said we have to be the cool fifth graders who help the little kids. I said we are already that, kind of.
entries.highlight: Lost to Jack at basketball, then learned his new jump shot and talked about being fifth graders.

entries.title: Spring Thunder close loss
entries.body: I had a soccer game after school. It is the spring Thunder season and Coach Mike made me a captain! I wear the armband. We played the Lightning, which is the best team. We lost but it was so close, two to one. I did not score but I made the pass to Mateo who scored our goal. After the game some kids on our team were mad and kicking the grass. I said guys, they are the best team and we almost beat them. That is good. Then I led the handshake line. Coach Mike told my mom I am a real captain. Last spring I would have been the one kicking the grass. Honestly, I remember that.
entries.highlight: Captained his soccer team in a close loss and helped upset teammates stay positive.

entries.title: Eli's birthday Mario Kart cup
entries.body: Today was Eli's birthday party and we had the Mario Kart tournament at his house. I made the bracket on a poster board, with the Biscuit bite mark copy on the corner as a joke. There were eight kids. I did the rules out loud at the start. Everybody plays four races per round, top two move on, and in the final no blue shells, Eli's rule. I lost in the second round to Owen. Not gonna lie, that was so surprising, but I said good game. Owen was so happy. The final was Eli against Jafie and Eli won on the last turn. Everybody went crazy. Eli's dad said I am a good tournament director. Then we had cake that looked like a racetrack. We played until the parents came, like three hours. Best party, honestly.
entries.favorite: Eli winning on the last turn
entries.highlight: Ran the bracket for Eli's birthday Mario Kart tournament and lost gracefully to Owen.

entries.title: Sleepover and the second level ramp
entries.body: Last night I slept over at Jack's house. In the afternoon before, me and Jack and his dad finished the second level of our bike ramp, the one we planned in March. It is like two feet now. We did it a bunch of times and I caught real air. Then for dinner we had tacos and we stayed up late watching a movie about a kid who becomes a race car driver. Jack fell asleep first for once. This morning his mom made pancakes, not chocolate like my dad, but blueberry, and they were really good. Do not tell my dad. We went back out and did the ramp again in our pajamas. Jack's mom took a video. I look so goofy.
entries.highlight: Finished building a taller bike ramp with Jack and slept over at his house.

entries.title: Jump rope unit in gym
entries.body: In gym we did not play dodgeball. We started the jump rope unit, which I thought would be for little kids. It is not. Coach Bell showed us the double under, where the rope goes around twice in one jump. I tried it like fifty times and kept hitting my ankles. Harper can do it ten times in a row. Then Coach Bell paired me with Caleb and we had to teach each other one trick. Caleb taught me the criss cross and I taught him how to jump faster. By the end I did two double unders! Just two, but last week I could not do any. My ankles have red lines on them. It is worth it. I am going to practice in the driveway tonight.
entries.highlight: Started jump rope in gym, traded tricks with Caleb, and landed his first double unders.

entries.title: I picked no screens myself
entries.body: No video games today, and Mom did not even say it. I decided by myself because we have a big soccer game Saturday and I want to practice my left foot shot. Coach Mike says I only shoot with my right. So after homework I went in the backyard and kicked the ball against the fence until it got dark, but only with my left foot. Tessa was the goalie for a while. She mostly ducked. Then Dad came out and played defense. I scored on Dad with my left foot three times. He said he let me, but I do not think so. Mom said she is impressed I picked practice over games. I said there is always tomorrow for games. That is something she says, so she laughed.
entries.favorite: Scoring on Dad with my left foot
entries.highlight: Chose on his own to skip games and practice his left-foot shot for an upcoming soccer game.

entries.title: Pizza after the left foot goal
entries.body: We had pizza for dinner, and it was a celebration pizza because I scored with my LEFT foot in the soccer game this morning! All that practice worked. It was from outside the box and it went in the low corner. Coach Mike yelled so loud. We won three to one. So we went to the pizza place with the arcade. I had seconds and then a breadstick. Tessa and me played the claw machine and she won a little frog. I spent six tokens and won nothing. The claw is rigged, I am sure of it. Dad said the claw machine is the Big Gary of arcade games. You never get it. That is so true it hurts.
entries.highlight: Celebrated scoring a left-footed goal in soccer with pizza at an arcade restaurant.

entries.title: May the Fourth Magic duel
entries.body: Today is May the Fourth, which is Star Wars day, so Dad wore his Star Wars shirt to dinner. After homework we played Magic the Gathering. Dad built a new deck that is all blue and it counters everything I play. It is so annoying. I lost the first game in like six turns. So I sat and thought about it, and I realized his counter spells cost a lot of mana. So I played two cheap creatures every turn instead of one big one. He could not counter them all. I won the next two! Dad said he is going to have to retire the blue deck. I said maybe just give it to Jack. He said you are a smart dude. Then we watched half of a Star Wars movie.
entries.highlight: Figured out a strategy to beat Dad's new counter-spell Magic deck by playing many cheap creatures.

entries.title: Kickball and the long kick
entries.body: In gym we played kickball outside because it was finally warm. I was on Jack's team. When it was my turn I kicked it so far it went over the kid in the outfield and I ran all the way home. A home run! Everybody on my team was screaming. Then the next inning I was the pitcher. Caleb kicked it right at me and I caught it, which was an out, but I felt kind of bad. He said nice catch though. Coach Bell said field day is in three weeks and kickball is one of the events. Jack said we are going to win field day for sure. I said we have to practice. Last year I did not even care about field day. Now I really want to win.
entries.highlight: Kicked a home run in gym kickball and got excited about the upcoming field day.

entries.title: Online Mario Kart with the whole crew
entries.body: I played Mario Kart for like six hours straight. Okay, not really, it was a Saturday and I had two hours. But it was the whole crew online at the same time, me, Jack, Jafie, Mateo, Owen and Eli, all in a private room. We talked on headsets and it was so loud. Mateo kept saying his internet was lagging every time he lost. Jafie used the cactus shortcut and everybody knows it now. Jack won the most races. I came in second overall. I said GG to everybody in the chat. That is what online people say. Then Mom said time and I said one more race, and she said one more race, and I actually stopped after one. She looked so shocked.
entries.highlight: Played online Mario Kart with all his friends and stopped after one more race as promised.

entries.title: Tessa's first card tournament
entries.body: Dad took me and Tessa to Game Haven for a Pokemon tournament, and this time Tessa played too! There is a little kids division for six and under. She is six and a half, so she just made it. I helped her build her deck all week. It has fire types and a Charizard I gave her. My old Charizard, the one from the fight with Jack in third grade. She won two games and lost two and got a participation ribbon. She would not take it off. I played in the big kids division and came in third out of twenty! Dale said the two of us are the Game Haven family now. Tessa said that she wants to be the champion next year. I believe her. She is stubborn.
entries.highlight: Helped Tessa enter her first Pokemon card tournament, gave her his old Charizard, and placed third himself.

entries.title: Racing Mateo with the laggy excuse
entries.body: Mateo came over after school and we played a racing game, the car one where you paint your car. I still have the flame car from third grade and the ugly Monster car. Mateo made his car look like Noodle, brown and long. We raced on every track. Mateo beat me on the city ones and I won on the desert ones. I kept asking if his internet was lagging since we were in the same room, and he threw a pillow at me. It ended six to six. Last year I made that tie with Jack and said ties are perfect. I still think so. Then we did homework together at my desk. Mateo said my homework spot is very professional. I said thank you, it has a lamp.
entries.highlight: Tied a racing game series with Mateo and then did homework together at his desk.

entries.title: Taco Tuesday on a Wednesday
entries.body: We had tacos for dinner, on a Wednesday, because Mom said Taco Tuesday is just a suggestion. I made my own tacos for the first time, I mean the meat and everything, with Dad watching. I browned the meat and put in the seasoning packet and the water. Dad only had to help with the stove knob. I put in extra cheese because I am the chef. Tessa said my tacos were better than Dad's. Dad said hey. Mom said I could be the taco chef every week now. I said only if I get paid. She said you get paid in tacos. That is actually a fair deal. The kitchen was really messy after though. I had to clean it. Chefs clean.
entries.highlight: Cooked taco meat for the family for the first time with Dad supervising.

entries.title: Owen's Minecraft museum
entries.body: After dinner Owen and me played Minecraft online together. We are building a museum on our server that has a room for every one of our big moments. There is a room for the Monster jump with a dirt ramp, a room for my birthday tournaments with trophies made of gold blocks, and a room for Owen's first Magic win with a giant wurm made of green wool. Owen is a way better builder than me because of all the Lego, so he does the walls and I do the signs and the details. We are going to add a room for Jack's ramp next. Owen said it is like a scrapbook but in Minecraft. That is honestly a really good idea. Then my timer went off and I logged off.
entries.highlight: Built a Minecraft museum of shared memories with Owen and logged off when his timer went off.

entries.title: Playoff loss to the Lightning
entries.body: I had a soccer game in the playoffs this morning. It was the Thunder against the Lightning again, the best team. It was so close. We were tied one to one until the very end, and then they scored on a corner kick. We lost two to one. Everybody on our team was so sad and some kids were crying, even Mateo. Not gonna lie, I was sad too. My throat got tight. But I remembered I am the captain, so I got everybody in a circle and said that we went from losing every game to the playoffs. Coach Mike said that was exactly right. Then we shook hands with the Lightning and I said good game to every single kid. One of them said you guys were the hardest team we played.
entries.highlight: Comforted his teammates as captain after a close playoff loss and shook hands with every opponent.

entries.title: Sad game pancakes for lunch
entries.body: After the playoff game Dad said we needed something to cheer us up, so he made chocolate pancakes for lunch, which is breakfast for lunch. It totally counts. And Tessa was so nice, she even gave me one of her pancakes because I was sad. That was really nice of her. I ate four and a half. Dad told me about when he was a kid and his baseball team lost the championship and he cried in the dugout. I did not know that. He said losing means you were in the big game. I thought about that a lot. Then we watched the game video Mom took, and honestly we played really well. I am still a little sad. But less sad.
entries.highlight: Felt better after a playoff loss when Dad made lunchtime pancakes and shared a story about losing.

entries.title: Rainy Pokemon Sunday
entries.body: It rained all morning on Memorial Day weekend, so Mom gave me extra Pokemon time. I finally finished the Pokedex in the new game! Every single Pokemon. Jafie still needs four, so I am going to help him trade for them. I named my last one, a little ghost type, Thunder, after my soccer team, because we did not win the playoffs but we were still good. Tessa watched me play and kept asking what every Pokemon was called. I told her all of them. She remembered like half. That is still a lot. Then the rain stopped and Dad said the rest of the day is a chore day. Uh oh.
entries.highlight: Completed his in-game Pokedex on a rainy holiday weekend and planned to help Jafie finish his.

entries.title: Building the garden boxes with Dad
entries.body: After the rain stopped, my chore was helping Dad build garden boxes in the backyard. It is way better than cleaning my room, which I did not even have to do today. Dad let me use the drill to put in the screws. You have to push really hard and go slow or it slips. I did eight screws by myself. Then we filled the boxes with dirt, which was a bajillion bags. Not really, twelve bags. Tessa planted strawberries and I planted peppers, the hot ones, for the Inferno wings challenge next year. Mom said we will see who can eat them. Dad said I am a real builder now, between the bike ramp and the garden boxes. My arms are so sore.
entries.highlight: Helped Dad build backyard garden boxes, using a drill himself and planting hot peppers.

entries.title: Memorial Day porch pancakes
entries.body: It is Memorial Day so there is no school. Dad made chocolate pancakes again on the griddle on the back porch, because it was sunny after all the rain. Two pancake days in one weekend is kind of the best. Tessa did not whine about anything. Instead she asked if she could flip one. Dad said only with help, so I helped her hold the spatula. She flipped it and it landed half on the griddle and half off. We all laughed and she laughed too. A year ago she would have cried about that for an hour. Then we went to the parade downtown and Tessa sat on Dad's shoulders. I can see over people now without sitting on anybody.
entries.highlight: Helped Tessa flip a pancake on Memorial Day and noticed how much calmer she has become.

entries.title: Field day champions
entries.body: Today in gym it was field day, the whole day outside! Our class was the green team. We did kickball, tug of war, the sack race, and the water balloon toss. I was partners with Caleb for the water balloon toss and we made it to the last three teams before it popped on his shirt. In kickball I kicked another home run. And in tug of war we beat Mr. Ortiz's class even though they had bigger kids, because Jack told everybody to pull at the same time on three. Our class won the whole field day! We got popsicles and a trophy for the classroom. Ms. Ruiz said this is the most teamwork she has seen in years. I am so sunburned. Totally worth it.
entries.highlight: Helped his class win field day through teamwork in kickball and tug of war.

entries.title: Fourth grade's last carpool Friday
entries.body: In carpool today everybody was singing really loud because it is the last Friday of fourth grade. We sang our song like nine times. Jack's mom said next year is our last year of carpool together, since in middle school we take the bus. Everybody went quiet for a second. That is weird to think about. Then Owen yelled that we should have one more song, and we all sang even louder. Mateo did the high part and his voice cracked, just like in third grade. Everybody remembered that. Nobody puked. Owen said that has been a whole year of nobody puking and he deserves a medal. Jack's mom said she will make him one. I hope she really does.
entries.highlight: Sang on the last carpool Friday of fourth grade and realized carpool will end after next year.

entries.title: Jack's yearbook drawings
entries.body: I went to Jack's house after school. We made a plan for summer on a big piece of paper, like our ramp plans. Stuff like the pump track every week, a Magic tournament, a sleepover at every house, and beating Jack's dad at basketball. Then we signed each other's yearbooks. Jack drew a picture of me as a giraffe even though he is the giraffe. I drew him as a shorty with a Pokemon card. Then his mom made root beer floats like last year when we did the cannonballs. We did not swim because the pool is still too cold. Jack said this was the best year of school ever. I said yeah, even though we had to do fractions. Especially because of fractions, actually. That is when I helped him.
entries.highlight: Made a summer plan and signed yearbooks with Jack, reflecting on a great school year.

entries.title: Last day of fourth grade
entries.body: Last day of school! No more homework, no more long division, and no more pacer test. Ms. Ruiz gave everybody a certificate and mine said Most Improved Mathematician. In September I got an 84 on times tables and now I am most improved. I did not even know that was an award. Jack got Best Leader and Caleb got Kindest Classmate. Ms. Ruiz hugged everybody at the door. She seemed strict at the start but she was honestly the best teacher I ever had. Speedy the turtle is going home with Harper for the summer. Summer is pump track every day, and this time I want to try the pro line, which is even bigger than the Monster. And a Magic tournament. And sleepovers.
entries.highlight: Finished fourth grade with a Most Improved Mathematician award and fond words for Ms. Ruiz.

entries.title: End of school burger night
entries.body: We had hamburgers and french fries for dinner to celebrate the last day of school. Dad grilled them in the backyard and I helped flip them, which is like flipping pancakes but heavier. I had a double cheeseburger and so many fries. Tessa finished kindergarten today too, so it was a double celebration. She got an award for best reader in her class! I said I taught her, which is kind of true, I listened to her read every night. Mom put both our awards on the fridge next to my 94 math test. Then we ate popsicles on the porch. Tessa said she is going to be a first grader and that is basically a big kid. I said not yet.
entries.favorite: Both our awards on the fridge
entries.highlight: Celebrated the end of school for both kids with a burger cookout and their awards on the fridge.

entries.title: Wings and the hot pepper report
entries.body: We had chicken wings for dinner on Sunday. Dad made them on the grill this time, with the honey barbecue sauce. I ate like nine wings. The hot peppers I planted in the garden boxes have little flowers now but no peppers yet. Dad said it takes all summer. I said the Inferno challenge will have to wait. Tessa's strawberries already have little green berries. She checks them every single morning in her pajamas. Then Mom asked everybody what they want to do this summer. I said land the pro line at the pump track, win a Magic tournament, and catch Big Gary. Dad said two out of three would be amazing. Tessa said she wants to ride her bike without training wheels. I said I will teach her.
entries.highlight: Shared summer goals at a family wing dinner and promised to teach Tessa to ride without training wheels.

entries.title: Summer league hat trick
entries.body: I had my first summer league soccer game today and I scored a goal! Actually I scored three goals, which is called a hat trick! One with my right foot, one with my head, and one with my left foot, the one I practiced so much against the fence. It was the best game of my life. Mateo passed me two of them. After the third one people threw their hats, not really, but everybody on the sideline was cheering. We won five to two. I made sure to pass to Caleb's little brother, who is on our team, so he could get a shot too. He missed but he was happy. Coach said the best players make everybody better. I want to be that kind of player.
entries.highlight: Scored a hat trick in summer soccer, including a practiced left-footed goal, and set up a younger teammate.

entries.title: Summer league at Game Haven
entries.body: Game Haven has a summer Pokemon league on Tuesday afternoons, so Dad dropped me off on his way back from lunch. It is the first time I went without Dad staying the whole time, and Dale said he would keep an eye on me. I battled Ruben, who is my rival now, but a friendly rival. We are tied in our all time record, like eleven to eleven. I counted. Today I beat him with a deck that uses a lot of switching. Then Ruben said he wants to team up for the doubles event in July. That is when two people share a side. I said yes right away. We shook on it. Dale said Game Haven doubles will never be the same. I think that is a compliment. I think.
entries.favorite: Ruben asking to be my partner
entries.highlight: Went to the card shop league without Dad staying, beat his friendly rival, and agreed to team up with him.

entries.title: Teaching Tessa to ride with Eli
entries.body: Me and Eli rode bikes around the neighborhood in the morning, but the real mission was Tessa. Dad took her training wheels off last night and she was scared. So me and Eli made a plan, like a coach plan. First she just walked the bike with her feet. Then I held the back of the seat and ran with her down our street. My legs were so tired. Eli ran on the other side to catch her if she fell. On like the tenth try I let go and she did not even know. She rode all the way to the stop sign by herself! When she found out I let go she screamed and then she crashed into the grass, but she was laughing. She did it six more times. She kept yelling Andy look! I was looking. I was so proud I almost cried, not gonna lie.
entries.favorite: Tessa riding to the stop sign
entries.highlight: Taught Tessa to ride her bike without training wheels with Eli's help, keeping the promise he made her.

entries.title: Thunder end of season party
entries.body: This afternoon we had the Thunder end of season party at Coach Mike's house. He has a pool and a big backyard. There was a cake that looked like a soccer ball and it was red velvet inside. Coach Mike gave everybody an award. I got the Captain's Award, which is a little gold trophy with a guy kicking a ball on top. He said I helped the team stay together, especially after the playoff loss. Mateo got Best Passer and he deserved it. Then we had a team water balloon fight and the parents joined in. Coach Mike got soaked. Then everybody signed a ball for him. I wrote thanks for making us good. My trophy is on my shelf now, right next to the Monster picture.
entries.highlight: Received the Captain's Award at his soccer team's end-of-season party.

entries.title: Party day chocolate pancakes
entries.body: Before the party Dad made chocolate pancakes for Saturday breakfast. I ate four, which ties my record, because I knew there was going to be swimming later and I wanted energy. That is my excuse. Tessa ate two and asked for a third, which has never happened. She said riding a bike makes her hungry now. She rode her bike around the cul-de-sac before breakfast, by herself, in her pajamas, with her helmet. Dad said that is a classic Saturday move. I showed Dad my new pancake trick, where I put the chocolate chips in a smiley face before flipping. Mine looked like a sad face because it bubbled weird. Dad ate it anyway. He said a sad pancake still tastes happy.
entries.highlight: Had Saturday pancakes with Dad while Tessa, newly riding, showed off her bike skills.

entries.title: Burger night with Grandma
entries.body: We had hamburgers and french fries for dinner because Grandma came over to visit. Dad let me be in charge of the grill timer, which is important because if you flip them too early they fall apart. I said flip at four minutes. Everything was perfect. I had a cheeseburger with pickles and so many fries. Grandma asked me about school, and I told her about the Most Improved Mathematician award. She said she always knew I was smart but I just rushed. That is what Mr. Dawson said in third grade! I guess I do not rush as much now. Then Tessa rode her bike up and down the driveway to show Grandma. Grandma clapped so hard. Tessa did not crash once.
entries.highlight: Ran the grill timer for a burger dinner with Grandma and told her about his math award.

entries.title: Summer room remake
entries.body: I had to clean my room. It took forever, but this time I wanted to, because I am making it a summer room. I took down some little kid posters, like the cartoon dinosaur one, and put up a poster of a BMX rider that I bought at the bike shop. I also moved my Magic cards into a new box with dividers by color. That took like an hour by itself. There were socks under my bed again, which is still a mystery after a year and a half. I am starting to think there is a sock portal. Tessa came in and asked for the dinosaur poster, so I gave it to her. She put it right above her bed. Now her room has my old stuff and my room has new stuff.
entries.favorite: Sorting the Magic cards by color
entries.highlight: Redecorated his room for summer and passed his old dinosaur poster to Tessa.

entries.title: My first Magic tournament win
entries.body: Dad took me to the Friday night Magic tournament at Game Haven for kids twelve and under. There were sixteen kids and it was a real bracket. I played my green deck with the spiders and the bears and the elves. I won my first game easy. The second game was so close, the kid had a flying dragon like Dad, and I blocked with a spider, just like I learned. In the final I played a girl named Sasha who is eleven and so good. We went to three games. In the last one I drew my giant bear right when I needed it. I won! I won the whole tournament! I got a pack of cards and my name on the whiteboard. I said good game to Sasha and she said you earned it. Dad hugged me so hard my hat fell off. One summer goal done.
entries.favorite: Drawing the bear right when I needed it
entries.highlight: Won his first Magic tournament at the card shop, beating an older player in the final.

entries.title: Back to the skate park with Tessa
entries.body: I went to the skate park on my scooter for the first time this summer and Tessa came too with her new scooter. My knee got scraped right away because I tried a tailwhip, which is where you kick the deck around in a circle. I fell but I got up. Then I spent most of the time teaching Tessa on the flat part, like how I started in third grade. She tried the little ramp, the same one I scraped my knee on that first April. She went down it and did not fall! I yelled so loud. A teenager said nice one, little dude, to her, which is exactly what one said to me. She said she is not little either. That made me laugh so hard. History repeats.
entries.highlight: Taught Tessa on the skate park's little ramp, the same one where he once scraped his knee.

entries.title: First look at the pro line
entries.body: We went to the pump track and I finally tried the pro line. It is the line on the far side with two jumps back to back, called a double. The first jump is like the Monster but taller and the landing goes right into the second jump. I tried just the first one three times and landed it. Then I tried the double and I did not have enough speed and I landed on the top of the second jump, which is called casing it. I fell once really hard and the wind got knocked out of me. I lay there for a second. But I got back up. Eli was there and he said I need to pump the berm harder. I have four weeks until July twentieth. That is my goal. Exactly one year after the Monster.
entries.highlight: Tried the pump track's pro line for the first time, fell hard on the double, and set a date to land it.

entries.title: Camping without screens
entries.body: No video games today because we went camping at the state park, and there is no signal anyway. We set up the tent and I did most of the poles while Dad held the corners. Last year I would have complained about no Switch the whole car ride. This time I brought my Magic cards and a flashlight and my BMX books. Me and Dad played Magic on the picnic table while Mom and Tessa went to the lake. Then we made a campfire and I roasted the perfect marshmallow, golden brown all the way around. Tessa set hers on fire every time, on purpose. At night we heard an owl. I lay in the tent and thought about the pro line and how to pump the berm harder. Not gonna lie, it was a really good day, even without a single screen.
entries.highlight: Went camping without screens, helped set up the tent, and played Magic with Dad by the campfire.

entries.title: Helping Jafie finish the Pokedex
entries.body: Not gonna lie, I played Pokemon for two whole hours this morning. But it was for a good reason. Jafie only needed four more Pokemon to finish his Pokedex, so we spent the whole morning trading on our Switches over at his house. Two of them I had extras of. The other two I had to go catch in the game, which took forever because one only shows up at night in the rain. When we got the last one, Jafie screamed so loud his mom came in to check if he was hurt. He said I am the greatest friend in history. I said I know, which is what I said to my cousin Danny when I was eight. But this time I was kind of joking.
entries.favorite: Jafie screaming at the last one
entries.highlight: Spent a morning trading and catching Pokemon to help Jafie complete his Pokedex.

entries.title: Library card club helper
entries.body: The library has a Pokemon card club for little kids on Thursdays in summer, and the librarian asked if I could be a helper because she saw me teaching Tessa. So I went and there were like ten kids, six and seven years old. I showed them how energy works, which is the thing Jafie's deck was missing in third grade. One kid kept making his cards talk to each other, just like Tessa used to. I did not tell him that is wrong. I said that is a cool story, and then here is how to battle. The librarian gave me a helper badge. Tessa was there too and she told everybody I am her brother like four times. I think I want to keep doing this all summer.
entries.highlight: Volunteered as a helper at the library's Pokemon card club for younger kids.

entries.title: Cousins Mario Kart cup
entries.body: The cousins came over for the Fourth of July weekend, so we did a big Mario Kart tournament. Me, Tessa, Danny, Benny, and two more cousins. Benny is five now and he is terrible, but he is so happy every time he finishes a race. I made the bracket so that Benny and Tessa were on teams with older kids, so it would be fair. Danny said that is a smart idea. Tessa and I were a team and we got second. Danny won. I said good game, he said good game. Then all the cousins went outside and did sparklers in the backyard. Benny licked a sparkler stick after it was out. Of course he did.
entries.favorite: Making fair teams for the little cousins
entries.highlight: Ran a family Mario Kart tournament and paired younger cousins with older kids to keep it fair.

entries.title: Building Jack a real deck
entries.body: Dad and me spent the evening building a Magic the Gathering deck for Jack's birthday in November. I know that is far away, but it takes a long time to pick the cards. Jack likes blue because of the sea monster from the first time he played. So we are making him a whole sea monster deck. Dad gave me some cards from his old boxes, and I used my tournament prize pack too. We tested it against my green deck and it beat me! That means it is good. Dad said I am the kind of friend who plans a present four months early. I said Jack is the kind of friend who deserves it, because he helped me land the ramp and he forgave me in third grade about the Charizard.
entries.highlight: Started building a Magic deck with Dad as an early birthday gift for Jack.

entries.title: Racing Eli on the new track pack
entries.body: Eli came over and we played a racing game. They added a new track pack, so nobody knows the shortcuts yet. Not even Jafie. We spent the first half hour just exploring the tracks to find secrets. Eli found a ramp that goes over a waterfall and I found a tunnel through a mountain. We agreed to share them with each other but not with anybody else, which is a secret alliance. Then we raced and Eli won seven to five. Honestly, I was not even mad. He drove better. We kept talking about the pro line instead because it is ten days until July twentieth. Eli said he will film it like he did the Monster. I said only if I land it. He said I will film it either way.
entries.highlight: Explored new racing game tracks with Eli and made plans for him to film the pro line attempt.

entries.title: Summer league heat wave game
entries.body: I had a soccer game on Saturday morning and it was so hot. Like ninety five degrees. The refs gave us water breaks every ten minutes. We lost but it was close, three to two. I scored one with my head off a corner, like my first header in third grade. On their last goal our goalie slipped. He was so sad, so I went and told him it was not his fault, the whole defense was tired. At the end I shook hands with everybody. Then I poured my whole water bottle on my head. Coach said I played like a captain even though it is summer league and I am not one officially. Then we went and got slushies. Blue raspberry, like after the last day of third grade.
entries.highlight: Scored in a close summer soccer loss on a hot day and comforted his teammate after a mistake.

entries.title: Bowl carving at the skate park
entries.body: I went to the skate park on my scooter in the morning before it got hot. I dropped in on the big ramp, which is the one bigger than the medium one. My legs did not even shake. Then I practiced carving in the bowl, which is when you go around the sides really fast in a curve. It is good practice for pumping the berm on the pro line, Eli said. Same idea. I did like twenty laps. Then I tried the tailwhip again and I landed one! Just one, out of maybe fifteen tries. My shins have scrapes from the deck hitting them. The teenager with blue hair is still there. He said you have grown so much. I did not know he remembered me from last year, when I kept falling off the little ramp.
entries.highlight: Practiced carving in the skate park bowl to prepare for the pro line and landed his first tailwhip.

entries.title: Burgers and the garden peppers
entries.body: We had hamburgers and french fries for dinner, and the first hot peppers from my garden box were ready! They are little and red. Dad sliced one and put it on my burger. It was so spicy my ears felt hot. I did not need milk though, so I think I am getting tougher since the Inferno wing. Tessa's strawberries are all gone because she ate them every morning. Dad said it is our first family harvest. I had two burgers. After dinner Tessa and me rode bikes around the cul-de-sac until it got dark.
