She can stand up on her pedals now, like I taught Owen last summer. I yelled pump the bumps and she did not know what that meant but she did it anyway.
entries.favorite: The first pepper from my garden
entries.highlight: Ate the first hot pepper from his own garden box and rode bikes with Tessa after dinner.

entries.title: Running the summer bracket
entries.body: Today was my summer Mario Kart tournament! It lasted like three hours. I invited Jack, Jafie, Mateo, Owen and Eli. I made a real double elimination bracket, which means you have to lose twice to be out, so it is more fair. I learned that at the Magic tournament. I wrote the rules on a poster. Random tracks, no repeat characters in a row, and the final is best of three. Mom said the poster looks very official. Owen made it to the final again, he is secretly so good now. Jack beat him. I came in third and I was fine with it. Everybody said it was the best tournament ever, and Jafie said I should run one every summer. I think I will.
entries.favorite: Everybody saying it was the best one
entries.highlight: Organized a fair double-elimination Mario Kart tournament for his friends and placed third.

entries.title: Landing the pro line double
entries.body: I did it! Exactly one year after the Monster, I landed the double on the pro line! The biggest jump ever. I was so nervous this morning I could not finish my pancakes. At the track I warmed up on the Monster three times. Then I went to the pro line. Eli had his phone out. I pumped the berm as hard as I could, like we practiced in the bowl, and I hit the first jump and flew and landed right on the back side and then I popped the second one and landed it clean. I screamed so loud the little kids I taught in March came running. Eli filmed it and then he filmed me yelling. Last year I could not believe I landed the Monster. This year I knew I could. That is the difference.
entries.highlight: Landed the pump track's pro-line double jump one year after his first big jump, with Eli filming again.

entries.title: Library helper day instead of games
entries.body: No video games today. It was actually not that bad. It was a library card club day, and I spent the morning helping again. There are new kids every week. Today a girl named Rosie cried because she lost, and I knew exactly what that feels like. So I told her that when I was nine I got so mad at losing that I unplugged a whole Switch and my friend went home. She stopped crying because she thought that was so funny. I said now I say good game, and she said good game to the kid who beat her. The librarian heard and gave me a thumbs up. Then at home I read my BMX book and drew a picture of the pro line for my wall.
entries.highlight: Helped a younger child handle losing at the library card club by sharing his own story about losing badly.

entries.title: Gary Junior, finally
entries.body: Dad took me fishing at the lake early in the morning when it was foggy, just like the day we saw Big Gary jump last summer. We used the frog lure I gave Dad for Christmas. Something grabbed it and pulled so hard the pole bent all the way down. This time I did not panic. I kept the line tight and reeled slow like Dad taught me. It took like five minutes. My arms were burning. Then Dad scooped the net and it was a giant catfish, like as long as my leg! Dad was yelling. It was not Big Gary, Dad said, it was too small. So we named it Gary Junior. We took a million pictures and let it go. Dad said the frog lure was lucky after all. I said patience. He laughed so hard.
entries.highlight: Reeled in a huge catfish on his own after years of fishing with Dad, nicknamed Gary Junior.

entries.title: Celebration Magic night
entries.body: At night Dad and me played Magic the Gathering to celebrate the catfish. We played three games on the back porch with the bug candle. Dad played his dragon deck, the old one, and I played my tournament green deck. I won two and he won one. Then Dad told me something cool. He said when he was ten he played Magic with his dad too, and his dad never let him win. I said you never let me win either. He said that is why it means something when you do. I thought about that for a while. Then Tessa came out and wanted to play, so we let her be on my team and she got to pick which creature attacked. She picked the bear. Good choice.
entries.highlight: Played celebratory Magic with Dad on the porch and let Tessa help choose his moves.

entries.title: Minecraft museum new wing
entries.body: Eli came over and we played Minecraft. We added a new wing to the museum that me and Owen started, because Eli wanted to be part of it. We built the pro line room with two dirt ramps and a block bike that looks like mine. And a lake room with Gary Junior made of gray wool and a little frog lure in his mouth. Eli made a pixel picture of the video he filmed, like a still frame, on a wall. It took forever but it looks so good. I won a little contest we did on who could build a fountain fastest. Eli said I am a museum genius. I said Owen did the walls. Being fair is important even when you are getting a compliment. Then we went outside to ride.
entries.highlight: Expanded the Minecraft memory museum with Eli, adding the pro line and the catfish.

entries.title: Monday catfish story pancakes
entries.body: Dad made chocolate pancakes on Monday because he took the day off to go see Grandpa. I ate four. Tessa told Grandpa on the phone the whole catfish story but she got it all wrong. She said it was an alligator and I wrestled it. I said that is not what happened, but Dad said let her tell it, it is a better story. So now in Grandpa's mind I wrestled an alligator. Then we drove to Grandpa's and I showed him the real pictures of Gary Junior. Grandpa said it was the biggest catfish he has seen in that lake in forty years. Forty years! He said Big Gary must be his great-grandpa. Everybody in my family has a Big Gary joke now. It is honestly kind of the family motto.
entries.highlight: Had breakfast pancakes, then showed Grandpa photos of his big catfish.

entries.title: Inferno challenge, garden edition
entries.body: We had chicken wings for dinner, and I did the challenge again but with my own garden peppers. Dad made a sauce out of them and it was even hotter than the Inferno wings. I ate a whole wing and I did not touch my milk for three minutes and ten seconds. A new family record. Dad tried one and he lasted one minute and then he was hopping around the kitchen. Mom said this is still not a real sport. Tessa made a sign that said ANDY IS SPICY. I put it on my shelf next to my Captain's Award. Then Mom made us all eat ice cream to cool down. I had seconds of the ice cream. That is the best part of a spicy challenge, honestly.
entries.highlight: Set a new family record eating a wing with sauce made from his own garden peppers.

entries.title: Room cleaning with a yard sale
entries.body: I had to clean my room, but this time there was a reward, because Mom said we are having a yard sale next weekend, so I could sell my old stuff and keep the money. That is a good deal. I went through everything. I found my old scooter that is too small, a box of Hot Wheels, and some games I do not play anymore. I put prices on them with stickers. I was going to sell my creeper box head but I could not do it. Some things are history. I found three missing socks, under the bed, as always. I put them in a bag and wrote MYSTERY SOCKS on it. Mom laughed. I am hoping to make forty dollars for the new Pokemon game coming out in the fall.
entries.favorite: Writing mystery socks on the bag
entries.highlight: Cleaned his room and priced old toys for a family yard sale to save toward a new game.

entries.title: Tessa's Mario Kart meltdown
entries.body: Not gonna lie, Tessa was really annoying today, but there is a twist. We had the yard sale in the morning, and I made thirty two dollars. Then in the afternoon me and Tessa played Mario Kart and she lost to me on Rainbow Road, and she threw her controller on the couch and said she quits and the game is rigged. She cried and stomped upstairs. I was mad at first. But then I realized that is exactly what I used to do. So I went upstairs and told her about Mateo and the blue shell and how I sat on the stairs. She said you did that? I said yeah, and that it is okay to be mad but you say good game anyway. She came back down and played again and lost again and said good game. Then she cried a tiny bit but it was progress.
entries.highlight: Helped Tessa through a sore-loser meltdown by telling her about his own past struggles with losing.

entries.title: Fishing with Tessa for the first time
entries.body: We went fishing on Monday, and this time Tessa came too. It was her first time. I showed her how to cast, and how to hold the pole so it does not fall in. She would not touch a worm, so I put it on for her, the same way Dad did for me before I learned. She caught a sunfish! It was tiny, like the one I caught when I was nine. She screamed and almost dropped the pole. Dad took a picture of the two of us with it. Then I caught a bass and she said it was too big and scary. We had our salami sandwiches. Tessa asked about Big Gary and I told her the whole story, from the very beginning. She believes in him completely.
entries.highlight: Took Tessa on her first fishing trip with Dad and helped her catch a sunfish.

entries.title: Racing game time trial grind
entries.body: This morning I did an hour and a half on the racing game and then went outside, because that is my own summer rule. I was trying to beat my own time trial record on the desert track, the one with the cactus shortcut. I kept almost doing it, like by a tenth of a second. It was so frustrating. In third grade I would have thrown the controller. Instead I watched my ghost car, which is the replay of my best run, and I saw that I was turning too late on the second curve. On the next try I beat it by almost a second. I texted Jafie a picture of my time. He said no way and went to try to beat it. Rivalry is back on.
entries.highlight: Studied his replay to beat his own racing game time trial record instead of getting frustrated.

entries.title: Skate park with the blue haired guy
entries.body: I went to the skate park on my scooter on Saturday. I dropped in on the big ramp and did a tailwhip off the little quarter pipe, my third one ever to land. Then the teenager with the blue hair, whose name I finally learned is Dante, showed me how to do a barspin, where you spin the handlebars around. It is so hard. I tried like twenty times and I did half of one. Dante said it took him a month. He goes to the high school and he said he started on scooter when he was nine too. I told him about the pro line and he said he saw the video, because Eli posted it on his mom's account. That is so crazy. Somebody I do not know saw my jump.
entries.highlight: Learned a new trick from an older skater at the park and found out he had seen his pro-line video.

entries.title: A long board game night
entries.body: No video games tonight because Mom wanted a family game night, and honestly it was actually fun. We played the sheep trading game and I taught Tessa how to trade, but fairly, not like when Dad used to trick her with the sheep. She won! First time ever. Dad said he has been defeated by a seven year old. She is not seven yet, she is seven next month, but she said she is basically seven. Then we played a card game called Spot It, where you find matching pictures, and Tessa is so fast at that one. I lost every round. I said good game every time like I was supposed to. It was a lot of good games. Mom made popcorn and we stayed up until ten.
entries.highlight: Taught Tessa to trade fairly at family game night, and she won the board game for the first time.

entries.title: Doubles event with Ruben
entries.body: Dad took me to Game Haven on Sunday for the doubles event, me and Ruben as partners. It got moved from July because of the store being repainted. We practiced on Tuesdays all summer. In doubles you have to talk to your partner about every move, which is hard when you are used to deciding alone. One time I wanted to attack and Ruben wanted to wait, and I said okay, your call, and his way was better. We made it to the semifinals and lost to two high school kids. Ruben was sad but I said we beat way more people than we lost to. Dale said we are the best kid team he has seen. Ruben and me used to be rivals. Now we are kind of friends. Weird how that happens.
entries.highlight: Played a doubles card tournament with his former rival and learned to trust his partner's decisions.

entries.title: Owen's growth spurt
entries.body: Owen and me played one on one at the park. Owen grew so much this summer, he is like as tall as Jack now. That is so not fair. Not gonna lie, everybody is growing except me. He does not even do the granny shot anymore, he has a real shot, kind of like Jack's. He beat me eleven to nine. I said good game and that he is a different person now. He said no, I just grew. We talked about fifth grade. Owen and me might be in the same class this time. The lists come out next week. We sat on the bench and drank Gatorade. Owen said he used to be scared to talk at lunch in third grade. I said I remember. Now he talks more than anyone.
entries.highlight: Played basketball with a newly tall Owen and talked about how much he has changed since third grade.

entries.title: Pancakes and class lists
entries.body: Dad made chocolate pancakes on Wednesday morning, because the class lists came out early! Tessa was bouncing in her chair because she has Mrs. Hart for first grade, who she wanted. I have Mrs. Kim for fifth grade. Owen is in my class! Mateo and Eli too! But Jack is not. Jack is in the other class with Jafie. Not gonna lie, I was kind of sad. At first I did not want to eat. But then Dad said you will still have carpool and lunch and the whole neighborhood. And Jack texted me that we are still the lunch table kings. So I ate four pancakes. I am still a little sad. But Owen and Eli and Mateo is a pretty good class.
entries.highlight: Learned he and Jack will be in different fifth-grade classes and felt better after talking with Dad.

entries.title: Pump track goodbye to summer
entries.body: We went to the pump track on Friday, the last big summer session before school. Today it was so crowded with kids trying to get one more ride in. The little kids I taught in March were there, and one of them landed the medium bumps with air! He looked at me right after like, did you see that. I gave him a thumbs up. Then I did the pro line double three times in a row without casing it. Eli and Owen were there too, and Owen tried the first jump of the pro line for the first time. He landed it! We were all yelling. Then we sat on the hill and ate popsicles and watched the sun go down. Best summer ever, I think.
entries.favorite: The little kid looking at me
entries.highlight: Finished summer at the pump track, landing the pro line repeatedly and cheering on a kid he once taught.

entries.title: Fifth grade desk upgrade
entries.body: I had to clean my room. The mystery sock bag did not get any new ones this time, which is a first. Mostly I set up my desk for fifth grade. I made a new homework whiteboard plan, like last year, but now it has more stuff because fifth grade has more homework. Monday to Thursday, homework then reading then games, Fridays free, and Sunday night check my backpack. I came up with that last part by myself. Mom saw it and said who are you. I said I am Andy. She said I know, I just mean you are so grown up. Then she got a little emotional. Moms are weird about school starting.
entries.highlight: Set up his desk and a self-made homework plan for fifth grade, which made Mom emotional.

entries.title: Eli's last day of summer
entries.body: I went to Eli's house for the last day of summer, because school starts tomorrow. We did not even play video games. We sat on his trampoline, which is new this summer, and talked about fifth grade, and the pro line, and what middle school will be like next year. Eli said he is nervous about middle school because it is huge. I said we will all be together, so it is fine. Then Biscuit tried to climb onto the trampoline and fell off, and we laughed so hard. Eli's mom made us burgers and we watched the video of my pro line jump and the Monster jump side by side. Not gonna lie, in the Monster one I look so little. Eli said you are still little. I said thank you very much.
entries.highlight: Spent the last day of summer at Eli's talking about fifth grade and comparing his jump videos from two summers.

entries.title: First day of fifth grade
entries.body: First day of school! I am in fifth grade now, the oldest grade in the whole school. Jack is not in my class this time, but Owen, Mateo and Eli are, and Jack and me saw each other at lunch right away. Our teacher is Mrs. Kim and she seems strict. She said fifth graders are leaders and she expects us to act like it. But then she told us she has a pet bearded dragon named Nacho, so she cannot be that strict. She asked us to write about something we are proud of from the summer. I had too many choices. I picked teaching Tessa to ride her bike, not the pro line. Mrs. Kim wrote nice job on it. Then at recess the little kids from the pump track waved at me.
entries.highlight: Started fifth grade with Mrs. Kim and chose to write about teaching Tessa to ride rather than his own jump.

entries.title: Riding to school with Jafie
entries.body: Today was the first day Mom let me ride my bike to school instead of carpool, because I am in fifth grade now. Jafie lives on the way, so we rode together. I had to text Mom when we got there. On the way home we went the long way past the pond. Jafie told me about his class, which has Jack too, and he said Jack talks about me all the time. That is funny. We stopped at the gas station and bought slushies with our own money. Mine was blue raspberry, of course. Then we rode up the Cedar Street hill with no hands for a second. Do not tell Mom about that part.
entries.favorite: Riding to school on my own
entries.highlight: Rode his bike to school with Jafie for the first time and stopped for slushies on the way home.

entries.title: Learning to do my own laundry
entries.body: After the bike ride my chore was laundry. Mom said fifth graders can do their own laundry, which I think is a made up rule, like the New Year's clean room rule from when I was eight. She showed me how the washer works. You sort lights and darks, you put in one pod, not three, and you pick normal. I put in my soccer stuff and my pump track clothes, which were so dirty the water turned brown. Then the dryer. Then I had to fold everything, which takes forever. I folded my shirts like a burrito. Mom said that is not folding. I said it is burrito folding. She let it go. Nothing shrunk. I am basically a laundry expert now.
entries.highlight: Learned to do his own laundry for the first time as a new fifth-grade chore.

entries.title: One hour Minecraft on a school night
entries.body: I played Minecraft for like six hours straight. Not really, it is a Monday so I had one hour after homework, like my whiteboard says. Fifth grade homework is already more, we had a math page and a whole science reading about the water cycle. But I did it first and then I went on the server with Owen and Eli. We started a new project, a giant castle for all of fifth grade, with a room for each kid in our class. Mrs. Kim's room is going to have a block bearded dragon named Nacho. Owen did the walls again because he is the wall guy. When my timer went off I said I have to go, and Eli said same. We are like a bunch of responsible people now. It is kind of funny.
entries.highlight: Played his school-night hour of Minecraft after homework and stopped on time with his friends.

entries.title: Rainy day carpool comeback
entries.body: It rained so hard this morning that Mom said no bike today, so I rode in carpool again. In carpool everybody was singing really loud, like it was a reunion. Jack yelled ANDY IS BACK when I got in. We sang our song from last year and everybody still knew every word. Jafie still made up the parts about pizza. Then Jack's mom said she misses me in carpool, which made me feel kind of good. Owen said we should have a rule that rainy days are carpool days for everybody. Everybody voted yes, six to zero. Jack's mom said she does not get a vote, apparently. Nobody puked, which Owen said is now a year and four months. Somebody please make him that medal.
entries.highlight: Rode carpool on a rainy day and had a happy reunion singing with his friends.

entries.title: Mateo's driveway three point contest
entries.body: Me and Mateo played basketball at his house after school, on the hoop in his driveway. Noodle sat on the porch in her sweater even though it was not cold, because she likes it. We did a three point contest, which Mateo's dad made by drawing a line in chalk. I made seven out of twenty. Mateo made five. Then Mateo's dad tried and made twelve, which is just showing off. He said he played in high school. We tried a game of two on one against him and we still lost. I said good game, Mr. Ramos. He said you two are getting good, and we said you are just old and tall, and he laughed. Then we did homework at Mateo's kitchen table. Mateo's mom checked it.
entries.highlight: Had a three-point contest with Mateo and his dad, then did homework together.

entries.title: The room inspection checklist
entries.body: I had to clean my room. It took forever, because this time I made my own checklist so I would not have to do it again in a week. The list says bed made, clothes in the hamper, desk clear, cards in boxes, floor visible. Floor visible is the hardest one. Under the bed I found my old flame helmet from third grade, which does not even fit on my head anymore. Then I gave Mom the checklist and asked her to inspect. She checked every box and gave me a sticker, as a joke, because the chore chart was from third grade. I put the sticker on my desk lamp. Then she said she is going to steal my checklist idea for Tessa. Tessa does not know what is coming.
entries.highlight: Made his own room-cleaning checklist and asked Mom to inspect his work.

entries.title: Tessa and my old binder
entries.body: My sister was a little annoying today. She went in my room when I was at basketball and took my Pokemon binder to show her friend Lily. When I got home they had all my cards out on her floor. I was about to yell, like old me, but then I saw they were actually playing a real battle with the rules I taught her. Lily did not know how, so Tessa was teaching her. Tessa looked so proud. So I just said you have to ask first next time, and she said okay, sorry. Then I sat down and helped them. Lily won a game. Tessa said good game to her. Her birthday is in nine days and she is going to be seven, and honestly she is less annoying every year.
entries.highlight: Found Tessa teaching a friend Pokemon cards with his binder and chose to help instead of yelling.

entries.title: Friday fishing and the middle school talk
entries.body: Friday fishing with Dad is kind of our thing now. The leaves are starting to turn and the lake was so calm. We had our sandwiches, which are now turkey because I said salami is for little kids. Dad said the frog lure is retired and hangs in the garage like a trophy, so we used a new spinner. I caught two bass and Dad caught a perch. Then Dad asked if I am nervous about middle school next year. I said a little bit, because Eli is nervous and it is huge. Dad said in middle school he made a new best friend and kept his old ones. He said that can happen. I like the fishing talks. Dad still says patience a lot. He is right, mostly.
entries.highlight: Fished with Dad and talked through his feelings about starting middle school next year.

entries.title: Fall Thunder, new kids
entries.body: I had a soccer game after school, and it is the first game of the fall Thunder season. A bunch of new kids joined who are younger, like third graders, because some of the old kids moved up to the travel team. I am captain again. We lost but it was close, two to one. The new kids are like we used to be in third grade, everybody chasing the ball like bees. So at halftime I told them to spread out and stay in their spots and pass. In the second half they did a lot better, and one of the new kids, Arlo, almost scored. After the game he said I was the best captain ever. I said wait until we actually win. Coach Mike said I sound like him now.
entries.highlight: Captained a younger fall soccer team in a close loss and coached the new kids at halftime.

entries.title: Setting up Tessa's seventh birthday
entries.body: My chore today was helping set up Tessa's seventh birthday party. She wanted a mermaid and karaoke party, of course, so I had to carry the karaoke machine outside and set up the big speaker from last Christmas. I also blew up like forty balloons. My face hurt. Then I did the scavenger hunt for her friends, with clues around the backyard, like the treasure hunt I made her when she was five and could not read. This time she could read every clue. She just was not allowed to because it was for her friends. I hid the prize behind the garden boxes. All the girls screamed when they found it. Then Tessa sang Let It Go on the karaoke for the four hundredth time. Some things never change.
entries.highlight: Helped set up Tessa's seventh birthday party, including a scavenger hunt like one he made when she was five.

entries.title: The barspin finally clicks
entries.body: I went to the skate park on my scooter on Sunday. My knee got scraped a little on the first try, but no big deal, I just kept going. Today I landed my first full barspin! That is the one Dante showed me in August where you spin the handlebars all the way around. It took a month, just like Dante said it took him. He was not there, so I had Jafie film it for proof. I landed it two more times after that. Then I tried a tailwhip into the bowl and fell on my butt, which did not hurt, like in third grade. Some things are exactly the same, I just do harder tricks now. Next time Dante is there I am going to show him. I bet he will say nice one, little dude.
entries.highlight: Landed his first full barspin at the skate park after a month of practice.

entries.title: Owen's sneaky racing skills
entries.body: Owen came over after school and we played a racing game. Owen is so good now, he says he practiced all summer while we were at the pump track. We did a ten race series and he won six to four. I said good game, and that he is a racing game genius now. He said he learned the cactus shortcut from watching Jafie. Everybody knows it. Then we did a team challenge against the computer on the hardest level and we beat it together, which is way more fun than racing each other, honestly. Owen said in third grade he never thought he would beat me at anything. I said in third grade I was a sore loser, so it was better he did not. He laughed so hard he snorted.
entries.favorite: Beating the hard level as a team
entries.highlight: Lost a racing series to Owen with good grace and beat a hard challenge with him as a team.

entries.title: My first week of dishes
entries.body: After dinner it was my turn to do the dishes, because Mom made a new chart where everybody has a night, even Tessa, who dries the forks. Tuesdays are mine. I rinsed everything and loaded the dishwasher, and I put the big pot in the sink to soak like Dad does. Tessa dried exactly four forks and then said she was done. I said that is not a whole job. She said it is a first grader job. That is actually kind of fair. I put on music on the speaker while I did it, the carpool song, and Mom danced a little in the kitchen, which was embarrassing. Then Dad said I loaded it better than him. That is not hard. Dad puts bowls in upside down.
entries.highlight: Took his first turn on the family's new dish-night chart and teased Dad about loading the dishwasher.

entries.title: The new fifth grade lunch league
entries.body: At lunch we battled with our cards. Fifth grade lunch is with both classes, so me and Jack can still sit together, which is the best part of the day. We started the lunch league again but bigger. There are nine people now, both Magic and Pokemon, so I made two divisions. Some fourth graders asked to watch, and Mrs. Kim said only if they are respectful, so now we have fans. I am the commissioner again and I keep the standings in a real notebook, not loose paper. Jack is in first in Magic and Jafie is in first in Pokemon. I am second in both. I did not change the numbers even a little. Jack says that is why everybody trusts me. Honestly, I think that is the best compliment.
entries.highlight: Restarted a bigger lunch card league in fifth grade and kept honest standings as commissioner.

entries.title: Pump track with Dante watching
entries.body: We went to the pump track on Saturday. Today it felt like the skate park came to us, because Dante from the skate park came to try it with his BMX. He is good at scooter but kind of bad at bikes, which made me feel better. I showed him how to pump the bumps without pedaling. He said I am a good teacher, like the little kids' mom said in March, and Owen in third grade. I did the pro line double and Dante said that is sick, little dude. I said I am not little. He said fine, medium dude. Then I showed him the video of the barspin and he gave me a fist bump. Today was a medium dude kind of day.
entries.highlight: Taught an older skater friend to pump at the pump track and showed him his new trick.

entries.title: Sunday tournament soccer
entries.body: I had a soccer tournament on Sunday at the big fields an hour away, the same one from last year. We lost but it was close in two games, both two to one, and we won the third game, three to nothing! It was the new kids' first win ever. Arlo scored his first goal and he ran around the whole field screaming. I remembered my first goal in third grade, the one between the goalie's legs. That is how he looked. I did not score today but I had two assists. After the last game the little kids dumped a cooler of ice water on Coach Mike. I helped plan that part. On the drive home I fell asleep with my cleats still on. Mom took a picture. Of course.
entries.highlight: Played a three-game soccer tournament where his young teammates got their first win and Arlo scored.

entries.title: Cleaning cleats and my room
entries.body: When we got home from the tournament I had to clean my room, because my soccer bag exploded all over the floor. There was grass everywhere, and my cleats were so muddy Mom made me clean them on the back porch with a brush first. Then I used my checklist. Bed made, clothes in the hamper, desk clear, cards in boxes, floor visible. Under the bed there were three soccer socks and none of them matched, so they went in the mystery sock bag. Now there are six. I think I should make a museum room in Minecraft just for the socks. Then I put my tournament medal on my shelf next to the Captain's Award. The shelf is getting so full. Mom says I need a second shelf.
entries.favorite: Adding to the mystery sock bag
entries.highlight: Cleaned his muddy cleats and room after the soccer tournament using his own checklist.

entries.title: The dodgeball catch for Caleb
entries.body: In gym we played dodgeball and I caught a ball and got Caleb back in. Caleb is in my class again this year. He has gotten so much faster since fourth grade, but he still gets out a lot. When I got him back in, he went and caught a ball right away and got two of our team back in. Everybody was cheering for him. It turned into a chain like the boys against girls game last year. We won. Coach Bell said our class has the best teamwork of all the fifth graders. Then he made me and Harper captains for next week. Harper said she is still going to aim at my face, just like last year. I said I would expect nothing less. She laughed.
entries.highlight: Caught a dodgeball to bring Caleb back in, starting a chain that helped his class win.

entries.title: Mateo's carpool remix
entries.body: Mateo made a remix of our carpool song on his tablet, with a beat and sound effects, like a car horn and a puking noise in honor of Owen. Owen said that is rude but he was laughing so hard. We played it like five times. Jack's mom made us turn it down because she could not hear the GPS. Then we talked about Halloween. Me, Jack and Jafie want to do a group costume this year, and Mateo said we should be the three Mario Kart guys. I said yes, I call Luigi. Jack called Mario. Jafie said he will be Toad because he is the shortest, and he said it before anyone else could. Respect.
entries.favorite: The puking noise in the remix
entries.highlight: Laughed at Mateo's remix of the carpool song and planned a group Halloween costume with friends.

entries.title: Fall leaves ride with Eli
entries.body: No school today because of the holiday, so me and Eli went on a bike ride that lasted like three hours. The leaves are all orange and yellow and we rode through the big piles on purpose. We rode the bike path all the way to the lake, the one me and Mateo did in March, and we saw the heron again. Or a different heron. They all look the same. Eli said middle school will have a mountain bike club and we should both join. That made me less nervous about middle school. Then we rode back and stopped at Eli's and Biscuit was so happy to see us that she knocked Eli over in the leaves. We laughed so hard. My legs are so tired.
entries.highlight: Took a long fall bike ride with Eli on a day off and learned middle school has a mountain bike club.

entries.title: Mario Kart costume testing
entries.body: Eli came over after school and we played Mario Kart. We did a whole series on the rainbow road, which is still the hardest track. At my ninth birthday Jack beat me on it and I hid in the bathroom. Today I beat Eli four out of six on it. Eli said good game and that I am a rainbow road master. Then I tried on my Luigi costume to see if I could play Mario Kart in it. The hat kept falling over my eyes and I drove off the edge. Eli was laughing so hard he fell off the couch. I said that is method acting. He did not know what that means. I do not really either, Mom says it about actors. Then we did our homework together at my desk.
entries.favorite: Driving off the edge in my costume
entries.highlight: Played Mario Kart with Eli on the track he once lost on at his birthday and tested his Halloween costume.

entries.title: Owen's Lego city is done
entries.body: I went to Owen's house on Sunday. Owen's brother is going to college next year, so he said the basement Lego city is officially Owen's now. Owen asked me to help finish the last part, which is a stadium that his brother started like three years ago. We built the seats and a scoreboard and little Lego players. Owen made the scoreboard say THUNDER 3 LIGHTNING 2, which never happened, but it is nice to think about. Pickles is old now and just slept on the beanbag the whole time. I remember the first time I came here in third grade, and Owen was so quiet at school. Not gonna lie, now he is like my second best friend, after Jack. Owen's mom made us grilled cheese, like that first time.
entries.highlight: Helped Owen finish his basement Lego city stadium and remembered his first visit in third grade.

entries.title: Giving away my first binder
entries.body: I had to clean my room. Two more socks went in the mystery sock bag, which is up to eight and still has zero matching pairs. But the big thing is I found my very first Pokemon binder, the one from third grade with the shiny Snorlax in the front. Most of the cards in it I do not use anymore. I was going to put it back on the shelf. But then I thought about the library card club kids, especially Rosie, who only had like twenty cards. So I decided to give the binder to the club so the kids can borrow decks. I kept the Snorlax, because it was the first good card I ever got, at Game Haven with Dad. Mom said that was really generous. I felt kind of grown up and kind of sad at the same time.
entries.highlight: Decided on his own to donate his first Pokemon binder to the library card club for younger kids.

entries.title: The health quiz in gym
entries.body: We had gym today, but instead of playing we had a health quiz, which is a gym thing in fifth grade. It was about the heart and why exercise is good for you. I got a good grade on my quiz, a 95! I knew the question about how many times your heart beats in a minute, which is like seventy for kids, because Coach Bell made us take our pulse after the pacer test. I also knew that sleep helps your muscles grow, which is a good reason why I should not stay up until one in the morning playing Smash. Do not tell Mom I said that. Then we got to play dodgeball for the last fifteen minutes, and I was the last one on, again. My heart was definitely beating more than seventy.
entries.highlight: Earned a 95 on a fifth-grade health quiz about the heart and exercise.

entries.title: Halloween as the Mario Kart crew
entries.body: Me, Jack and Jafie went trick-or-treating together, with no parents walking with us at all this year, just our phones to text. We were the three Mario Kart guys, I was Luigi, Jack was Mario, and Jafie was Toad. We even had cardboard karts around our waists with straps. First we took Tessa and Lily around our street, because Mom asked, and Tessa was Princess Peach, so she matched us. She said she is on my team, like in Mario Kart. Then we dropped them home and did the whole neighborhood plus the cul-de-sac with the full-size candy bars. After, we dumped everything on my floor and traded candy. I traded my candy corn for Jack's peanut butter cups, like last year. A Halloween tradition. Mateo would say wait a day. Not for candy.
entries.highlight: Trick-or-treated in a Mario Kart group costume with Jack and Jafie, after taking Tessa around first.

entries.title: Halloween morning at the pump track
entries.body: Before trick-or-treating, in the morning we went to the pump track. I went over the big bumps without pedaling and did the pro line twice. It was so cold my fingers were stiff, and the dirt was wet from the rain, but it was perfect for the berm. A bunch of people came in costumes, which was so funny. There was a kid dressed as a banana on a BMX. I did not wear my Luigi costume because the hat would fall in my eyes, like when I tried playing Mario Kart in it. Eli wore cat ears on his helmet. The little kids I taught in March are all doing the medium bumps now. One of them asked me to watch him do it. I did. He landed it and said happy Halloween.
entries.highlight: Rode the pump track on Halloween morning and watched a younger kid he taught land the medium bumps.

entries.title: Basketball unit finally
entries.body: We had gym today. It was boring until the end, because the first half was stretching and learning the rules of basketball, which everybody already knows. But at the end we got to play real games, five on five. Coach Bell put me with Caleb and Harper. I did the spin move that Eli taught me in third grade and scored. Then I passed to Caleb in the corner, like the play me and Eli figured out at the rec center, and he made it! It was his first basket ever in gym. Everybody went crazy, even the other team. Harper said that was a great pass. Coach Bell said I am a pass first point guard. I asked if that is good. He said it is the best kind. Honestly, I kind of like passing more than scoring now. Not always. But a lot.
entries.highlight: Set up a classmate for his first gym basket and was called a pass-first point guard.

entries.title: Cold November catch
entries.body: Dad took me fishing at the lake after school on Friday. It is getting so cold again, like the first time Dad told me about Big Gary, almost two years ago. We brought the thermos with hot chocolate, which is a tradition now. I caught a big perch, and Dad caught a bass, and we let them both go. Then I told Dad about the binder I gave to the library and about running the Smash tournament. Dad said he has noticed I am different than when I was eight. I asked how. He said I used to want to win everything, and now I want everybody to have fun. I said I still want to win. He said I know, that is fine, you just do it nicer. That is a good way to say it.
entries.favorite: Dad saying I win nicer now
entries.highlight: Went cold-weather fishing with Dad, who told him how much he has grown since he was eight.

entries.title: Wings and Jack's birthday deck
entries.body: We had chicken wings for dinner on Saturday, and I had seconds of the honey barbecue and one garden pepper wing, just to prove I still can. Dad and Tessa did not even try. While we ate I showed everybody Jack's birthday present, which is finally finished. It is the sea monster Magic deck me and Dad started in July. I put it in a deck box with a sea monster drawing I made on the lid, and wrote a note inside that says to the giraffe, from shorty. His birthday party is next weekend. Tessa asked if she could give him something too, so she drew a picture of Jack as a giraffe playing cards. Mom said we are both very thoughtful. I said that is because Jack is the best. It is true.
entries.highlight: Showed his family the Magic deck he spent months building for Jack's upcoming birthday.

entries.title: Carpool singing
entries.body: In carpool today everybody was singing the same song really loud, Mateo's remix version, even Jack's mom a little bit. It was raining, so I was in carpool instead of riding my bike, which is our rainy day rule. Jack kept poking me in the side during the whole song and it was annoying but kind of funny, because every time he poked me I sang the wrong word. I poked him back and then Mateo poked both of us and Jack's mom said hands to yourselves, boys. Owen sat in the front like always now. Nobody puked in the car this time. Owen said that makes it almost a year and a half and he is still waiting for that medal. Jack's mom said it is coming. I do not think it is.
entries.highlight: Sang loudly with friends in a rainy-day carpool while Jack kept poking him.

entries.title: Chocolate pancakes
entries.body: Today I woke up and it was sunny, which was so nice after all the rain this week. Dad made chocolate pancakes for breakfast and I ate three. I used to eat four, but I think three is the perfect amount now because then I am not too full to play. My sister did not throw a fit at all. She did not throw a fit at all last week either, so I think she is growing out of it. She even poured her own syrup without spilling. I did not have to do any chores, because it is Saturday and my checklist room was still clean, so I played frisbee in the backyard with Dad and Tessa. I threw one so far it went over the fence and Dad had to go get it from the neighbor.
entries.highlight: Ate chocolate pancakes on a sunny Saturday and played frisbee in the backyard with Dad and Tessa.

entries.title: Pump track with my bike
entries.body: We went to the pump track. It is kind of like a skate park made of dirt for bikes. Tessa came this time to watch, and she brought her own bike to try the little kid loop. I went over the big bumps without pedaling, just pumping with my arms and legs, the way Eli taught me before I landed the Monster and the way I taught the little kids in March. It is so much fun when you get the rhythm right. I fell one time on the berm turn, because the dirt was loose from the rain, but I got back up. My elbow is a little scraped. Then Tessa did the small loop three times. She pedaled the whole time, but that is how you start. I said next year she can pump.
entries.highlight: Rode the big bumps at the pump track, fell once and got back up, while Tessa tried the little loop.

entries.title: Sleepover party
entries.body: I had a sleepover with my friends Jack and Jafie. We had pizza for dinner, like a bajillion pizzas (not really, just two). Mom said that is my joke from my ninth birthday and I said it is a classic. We had pepperoni and cheese, and Jafie ate the most, which nobody expected. Then we had a dance party in the living room with Mateo's remix of the carpool song and Tessa's karaoke speaker. Tessa danced with us for two songs and then Mom said bedtime for first graders. We stayed up late, like midnight, talking about middle school and who has the best Smash character. It was kind of like a birthday party but even better, because nobody had to be the birthday person. Everybody was just there.
entries.highlight: Hosted a sleepover with Jack and Jafie featuring pizza, a dance party and staying up late.

entries.title: Video game tournament
entries.body: The morning after the sleepover we had a Smash Brothers tournament. I made a little bracket on my whiteboard, a round robin so everybody plays everybody, which is the most fair with three people. I won two rounds and Jafie won the rest. Jafie is honestly so good with the sword guy now. I said good game to Jafie and he said good game back. Jack did not win any but he said he had the most fun, so he is the fun champion. I made him a little trophy out of a cereal box. Then Mom said we had to go outside after that, and we did not even argue, because we wanted to ride to the pump track anyway. Two years ago I would have begged for one more round.
entries.highlight: Ran a fair round-robin Smash tournament after the sleepover, won two rounds, and happily went outside.
